### Public authoring and readout

Authoring uses molla_sim::runtime::RigidScene and opaque handles. DistanceLimits,
SphericalConeLimits and JointBreakLimits have independent Option<Real> fields;
set_distance_limits/distance_limits,set_cone_limits/cone_limits and
set_joint_break_limits/joint_break_limits provide fallible mutation and readback.
joint_broken and repair_joint expose persistent break state and explicit repair.
FrictionCoefficients is an explicit ContactMaterial.friction pair, authored through
ColliderDesc and scene collider replacement; None preserves the scalar fallback.

RigidWorld::from_scene selects CPU; from_scene_gpu selects a supplied Engine.
set_reaction_readout,joint_reaction,joint_reaction_samples,distance_reading,
cone_reading and joint_break_events/drain_joint_break_events expose solved data.
Missing/stale/disabled readout is None, not a fabricated zero load. Forces are N,
torques Nm in world coordinates about authored joint anchors; substep samples and
peaks are separate from frame means. Break thresholds compare physical substep
loads inclusively, trigger once per episode and detach at a safe boundary without
resetting physical motion. Event draining is not repair.

Friction solves coupled contact stick/slip: static response remains inside the
static disk; sliding uses the dynamic disk and relative surface velocity. Authoring
requires finite0<=mu_dynamic<=mu_static and never silently clamps. An explicit pair
overrides the legacy scalar; absent pair maps the scalar to equal coefficients.
Pair combination applies independently with Average<Min<Multiply<Max priority.

GPU validation rejects articulations above32 joints, unknown motor models,
unsupported external kinds and unsupported coupled non-scalar bounds. The current
bound check accepts Revolute,Prismatic,D6 and Ball; the older matrix excluding
Ball intervals is stale. Fixed capacities abort rather than truncate. Positive
parameters not representable in f32 can be rejected explicitly. These are
capability boundaries, not silent CPU fallback.

Live GPU route: scene authoring/compiler -> GPU model/control upload on rebuild
-> retained Featherstone state ping-pong -> device distance/cone/loop/contact
response -> device reaction and break reduction -> compact break notification
and safe topology rebuild -> frame readout/finite checks -> scene commit.
Host validation, sleep selection, topology orchestration and frame publication
remain CPU work; they are not a whole-scene per-step CPU physical solve.

The active rigid GPU lane uses ResidentNarrowPhase: packed primitive kinds0–6
are supported; RoundCylinder, hull/convex parts, triangle meshes and heightfields
are not GPU collision substitutes. ModelBuilder packs them with sentinel0xff;
an admitted pair faults in narrow_gjk rather than falling back to host contacts.
Disabled/excluded/nonoverlapping unsupported shapes need not produce an admitted
pair. The separate legacy/hybrid geometry API's fallback behavior is not this
production lane. CPU collider authoring retains each explicit representation.
Mass calculations use analytic/mesh volume integration, additive convex pieces,
zero volume for heightfields, and the documented inner-cylinder approximation
for rounded-cylinder mass. These are declared boundaries, not full GPU mesh
collision certification or exact rounded-volume claims.

Source tracing finds a concrete allocation defect in rigid_contacts_gpu.rs:
per-island width adds the entire scene's scalar row count. Response gram storage
multiplies island slots by width twice, producing cubic scene-size growth for
many otherwise independent constrained articulations. The repair will bound
joint rows by actual base constraint components reachable through the configured
physical contact count, while retaining every original global row/index and all
constraints. Impact and position island packers must enforce that same physical
contact limit, independently of total joint/contact block width. Over-capacity
graphs remain explicit errors, not truncated solves. No numerical tolerance,
fixture size, substeps or measured-frame count will be reduced.

The GPU validator also rejects unsupported active loop kinds, unknown motor
models and unsupported finite-axis-bound/contact combinations. These limits are
source-verified in `rigid_world_gpu.rs::validate`, not claims that every accepted
combination has passed final certification. Core units are metres, kilograms,
seconds, radians, newtons and newton-metres. Stale/unsolved readout is None, not a
zero physical load: readouts require the solved DynamicsStamp. Legacy public
CRBA/RNEA analysis zeros equality-locked columns/efforts; physical response and
wrench reconstruction retain partial angular support. The source-grounded next
Gearbox signatures are in `MOLLA_PRIMITIVES_HANDOFF.md`; no Gearbox edits were made.

Friction validates finite `0 <= mu_dynamic <= mu_static`; an authored dynamic
coefficient larger than the static coefficient is rejected, not clamped. None
for the explicit pair maps the legacy scalar to both regimes. Pair rules apply
componentwise, with rule priority Average < Min < Multiply < Max. Static holding
depends on a coupled impulse solve, not a zero-load stationary body. The runtime
contact readout includes regime, applied coefficient and tangential impulse.

The cone setting accepts finite half-extents from zero through pi inclusive.
Distance settings accept independent finite nonnegative bounds; coincident
positive-radius bounds use the documented stable-handle-oriented world-X normal.
Break thresholds are inclusive; zero breaks on a valid zero-load sample, while
`None`/positive infinity disables a channel. Reaction loads are world-space N/Nm
at the authored endpoint anchors; mean loads and substep peaks are distinct.
These are source-verified contracts, not newly measured physical acceptance.

GPU runtime validation currently accepts rigid and compliant external
Fixed/Revolute/Prismatic/Ball/D6 loops plus Distance. It rejects other active
external kinds, articulations over 32 joints and unknown motor models. With
shapes present, unlocked finite tree-axis bounds are supported on scalar joints,
D6 and Ball; the older support snapshot's omission of Ball is outdated.
Registered actuator/wheel/track GPU stepping and CPU automatic breaking with
registered devices remain explicit unsupported paths, not hidden CPU fallback.
No Gearbox files or USD model assets are edited by this work.

### Engine-local immutable GPU programs — implementation, 2026-10-01

The previous goal turn made concrete implementation/evidence progress. Current
source and process revalidation finds no inherited live owned handle. To avoid
recompiling identical Featherstone shader/layout programs for every world, choose
an Engine-owned typed,64-entry bounded LRU cache; compiler variants include both
joint scratch capacity and mixed-stop row capacity. Retain only immutable pipeline
and layout handles. Every kernel must still allocate its own model/state/control,
status, CSR, precision, activation and readout buffers. No physics law, supported
model family, step count, tolerance or shader source is changed by this design.

Initialization is serialized per Engine, errors/failed factories are not cached,
and validation/allocation/internal error scopes are checked before retention.
Logical-device destruction clears the cache. Device-only constructors stay
uncached and keep their existing signatures. Different Engines never share cached
objects, including wrappers for external devices. This is implementation in
progress, not a demonstrated speedup, broad GPU pass or completed plan.

#### Antipodal cone limiting chart — bounded CPU/GPU runtime checks, 2026-09-30

CPU/GPU cone geometry now has a deterministic limiting chart within the existing
antipodal sine floor 1e-6. It selects the widest transverse extent, treating a
disabled extent as pi and selecting the first axis on ties. For a finite maximum
extent below pi, the inward row uses angular separation minus that extent and a
unit radial direction projected orthogonal to the child primary direction. This
is a one-sided cut-locus row, not a claimed unique smooth logarithm Jacobian.
The other zero extent uses its exact transverse-plane angular residual/Jacobian;
two zero extents retain two bilateral rows. An admissible antipode with a disabled
or pi-wide direction gets no artificial radial stop. Away from this neighbourhood,
ordinary finite cones with both extents below pi retain their original disk-log
ellipse and row order outside the immediate antipodal neighbourhood.

For a disabled or authored-pi extent, the antipode is itself admissible. Ordinary
geometry now selects its short geodesic return row when `pi-theta` is smaller
than the radial ellipse/zero-extent violation. Its exact angular derivative is
`-p cross (t/s)`. This avoids an artificial multi-radian impulse near an
admissible pole just because the ordinary logarithm chose a forbidden azimuth.
Reported violation is the smaller of those two recovery-branch distances for
these wide cones; the admissible set is unchanged. The new unit checks row
direction, error and one-sided finite-difference behavior.

The replacement has the focused evidence below. General outgoing velocities at
admissible anisotropic antipodes and neighbourhood/ordinary-chart transitions
still require broader acceptance; no full singular-cone certification is claimed.

#### Coupled tree velocity feedback — bounded CPU/GPU checks, 2026-09-30

CPU `joint_drives` and GPU `featherstone_feedback` used 64 projected
Gauss–Seidel sweeps and returned without checking convergence. Strongly coupled
positive-definite inertia responses can converge too slowly for that fixed
count. Replaced CPU feedback with the existing diagonally normalized bounded
active-set solve; GPU now factors normalized free-variable systems, hits force
bounds, and releases bounds by the KKT gradient. Pivot/non-finite failures or
iteration exhaustion return the existing numeric error instead of silently
publishing a truncated solve. No force cap, brake exclusion, motor-model scope
or device-capacity guard changes.

The new fixture uses xy inertia `[[1,0.999],[0.999,1]]`, with weak/common
principal moments 0.001/1.999. Its orthogonal moment must be 2.0, not 1.0:
positive definiteness alone is insufficient for physical rigid-body inertia;
the principal moments must also obey triangle inequalities. The initial fixture
was correctly rejected during scene construction and has been corrected without
changing the xy response, motor inputs or rate tolerances. GPU helper arguments
also now use the same explicit WGSL aliases as their local variables, resolving
the initial Naga pointer-type mismatch without disabling validation.

selection previously ignored bounds, unlike the exact-pole phase path.

physical direction. The GPU scalar row reuses existing transverse metadata for
the pitch interval and its low residue, preserving the 240-byte row layout.

deferred projection selects its chart using all authored bounds but clamps only
locks. D6 angular intervals select a periodic orientation chart, not an
accumulated-revolution state. Mixed angular locks, arbitrary repeated crossings
and all actuator torque semantics remain uncertified.

#### Nonorthogonal articulated contacts — 2026-09-30

`runtime_loop_articulated_contacts.rs` adds an independent integrated oracle
for nine two-body assemblies: a world-rooted inclined prismatic joint, a fixed
descendant, two separate sphere/floor contacts, and a rotated external compliant
D6 link applying forces at an off-centre descendant anchor. Mass pairs are
[s, 3s] for s = 0.01/1/100 kg; effort caps are 0/0.25/infinite multiples of
assembly mass. The permitted tree axis [0.8, 0.6, 0] has nonzero projections
onto both the normal and both driven loop directions, so contact pressure and
the loop feedback/effort genuinely share the same articulated response.

The analytic oracle derives the effective scalar mass, coupled bounded effort
and implicit feedback impulses, explicit pressure/damping recurrence and
semi-implicit trajectory. Newton/Euler balance independently derives child and
parent anchor wrenches for the root, fixed descendant and external link,
including the fixed lever and off-centre loop-arm torque. Every substep sample,
anchor, mean, peak, contact normal impulse, both body trajectories and invalid
body count is checked. Six 60/120/240 Hz × 1/4-substep settings run sixteen
frames, with motor, frame, softness, cap and disable/re-enable edits. Balanced
startup loads establish a persistent contact episode before force edits.
Declared CPU/GPU tolerances are 1e-8 / 2e-4 with an explicit assembly-mass
absolute floor for force/torque cancellations; they are not tuned after failures.

`molla-kernels::CompliantLoopKernel` adds retained device row generation for the
existing compliance law. Requests carry authored endpoint frames, linear/angular
axis, locked/bounded interval or motor feedback, force cap and effective-mass
scaling. Outputs contain signed coordinate error/rate, each body's world COM

differences. Inactive rows are cleared, not left with previous-frame data.

by the request constructors. Invalid device endpoints/axes or nonfinite generated
rows raise the dedicated bit-15 fault; bits 16–29 are already used by contact paths.

three rates satisfy the plan's 1e-3 m ten-second displacement gate. This test is
now in `PRIMITIVE_GPU_BASELINES`. Strict workspace clippy and formatting pass in
`quotient-predictor-psd-clippy.log` and `quotient-predictor-psd-fmt-check.log`.

Next verification is serialized: full distance regressions, the four previously
unreached aggregate lanes, refreshed full GPU aggregate, then hardening only on
success. Each stage writes its own `.exit` status. No source edits or external
benchmark rebuilds are planned while this sequence runs.

## Current live-runtime support snapshot

Source-audited on 2026-09-30. This supersedes the historical bridge matrix below.
"Implemented" identifies a live code path, not completed physical certification.
Earlier aggregate/example results predate recent changes and are not current
full-worktree acceptance. Current device evidence includes the three bounded
one-frame reversed-D6 fixtures, both exact XYZ pole fixtures, the expanded
three-route contact-wake case and retained hot-gain wake/force case at the top.

| Capability | CPU `RigidWorld` | GPU `RigidWorld` | Open boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rigid distance, world/body and external links | Implemented | Retained device response and publication implemented | Current physical/scale/resource gates; full primitive performance matrix |
| Geodesic swing cones and ball anchoring | Implemented | Tree/external cone and anchor paths implemented | Current loaded/free-twist/contact/antipodal and scale gates |
| Rigid Fixed/Revolute/Prismatic/Ball/D6 external loops | Implemented | Retained axis/ball response implemented | Current mixed contact/control/reaction/break acceptance |
| Compliant Fixed/Revolute/Prismatic/Ball/D6 external loops | Coupled force response implemented | Retained loop geometry/mass/Jacobian/solve/loads implemented | Recent one-frame D6 fixture passes; broader kinds and sustained acceptance remain |
| General reactions and automatic break | Samples, means/peaks, detachment and rollback implemented | Device recovery/reduction/thresholds and transactional continuation implemented | Current analytic/mixed/threshold/rollback gates; registered-device restrictions below |
| Static/dynamic friction and restitution | Implemented, historical physical fixtures recorded | Retained contact/impact/material/unified response implemented | Current holding/sliding/energy/manifold/sleep/resource acceptance |
| Tree/loop motors, brakes and speed caps | Implemented | Device feedback and coupled cap rows implemented | Recent D6 one-frame wiring passes; every axis/mode/load/mutation combination is not certified |
| D6 compliant tree limits | Implemented | Mass-scaled device spring response implemented | Active reversed-D6 one-frame fixture passes; equilibrium/energy/scale gates remain |
| D6 singular XYZ coupled bounds | Bound-aware phase chart implemented | Shared chart and phase response rows implemented | Both exact-pole active one-frame fixtures pass; mixed locks, crossing and sustained numerical gates remain |
| Reversed tree dynamics and floating momentum | Authored signed frames implemented | ABA/FK/Jacobian/CRBA/reaction/transport paths implemented | Transport bug fixed; three one-frame cases pass, broader constrained/scale gates remain |
| Body damping | Full-tensor mass-weighted loads implemented | Retained hot coefficients and active-body loads implemented | Nonzero damping participates in recent fixtures; isolated/sleep/edit/scale gates remain |
| Public usage examples | Six example cases implemented, historical runs recorded | Same public API, explicit GPU selection | Current rerun and final return-package acceptance remain |

Current GPU capability checks in `crates/molla-solvers/src/rigid_world_gpu.rs`
explicitly reject:

- External joint kinds other than Distance or Fixed/Revolute/Prismatic/Ball/D6.
  The latter five are accepted both rigid and compliant. Do not retain the old
  claim that general rigid loops or compliant Ball are still rejected.
- Articulations exceeding 32 joints (not a 32-articulation world limit).
  This guard bounds shader-private arrays; removing it is not a capacity upgrade.
- Unknown motor-model values. Force/acceleration feedback, tree/loop brakes,
  body damping and reversed trees have implementations, not blanket guards.
- When the model contains shapes: finite unlocked axis bounds on non-scalar
  tree kinds other than D6. Equality locks remain allowed; hinge/slider and D6
  translation/angular intervals and generalized speed caps now have coupled
  implementations. Singular XYZ now has a coupled phase-chart implementation,
  not the former blanket singular-chart rejection. This validation is
  model-wide, not conditional on whether the bounded joint is touching a collider.
- Registered actuator devices, wheels or tracks during GPU stepping. Contact
  sleeping/collision wake-up is now integrated and has focused passing fixtures;
  broader history, mutation and mixed-constraint certification remains open.

CPU automatic breaking also rejects registered devices/wheels/tracks
(`rigid_breakage.rs`). These guards are remaining implementation boundaries, not
permission to silently substitute CPU execution or count unsupported combinations
as complete. `RigidScene` does not compile runtime Cable tree joints; lower-level
Cable/FEM support is not certified by this package. Positive GPU parameters may
also be rejected when their f32 representation overflows or underflows, and
contact/island storage overflow aborts transactionally rather than truncating.

Logical transfer, Rust allocator and observed device-allocation metrics are
implemented, but current measurement acceptance remains open. Device-internal
transient peak allocation is explicitly unavailable; observed allocation-event
peaks must not be relabeled as that metric. Current full workspace/hardening,
physical, scale/performance and final handoff gates remain incomplete.

### Backend handoff surface — source inventory, not acceptance

#### Initial bulk construction — source checked 2026-10-01

`RigidSceneBuilder::new() -> RigidSceneBuilder` stages initial authoring without
intermediate dense models. `insert_body(BodyDesc)`, `insert_collider(ColliderDesc)`
and `insert_joint(JointDesc)` return the same opaque handle types as RigidScene.
It also supports initial gravity, distance/cone bounds, per-axis bounds and motors.
`build(self) -> Result<RigidScene>` consumes authoring and validates/compiles once;
invalid geometry/topology returns no partial live scene. Handles resolve in the
returned scene, whose revision starts at0 and whose body/component/contact
identity stamps are initialized. It is not a live batch-edit API: state mutation,
external-loop authoring and other controls still use existing live methods after
build. Existing live edit rollback, retained state/controls and handle allocation
remain unchanged; the benchmark uses this initial construction path.

#### Geometry authoring inventory — source checked 2026-10-01

`ColliderGeometry` is an explicit representation choice. `runtime.rs::add_shape`
maps these variants to their matching builder shape, not a generic box/sphere
substitute. This table is a source contract, not CPU/GPU certification of every
collision pairing or mass-property calculation.

| Runtime geometry | Authoring data and compiled representation |
|---|---|
| Ball | Radius; sphere shape |
| Cuboid | Three half-extents; box shape |
| Capsule | Half-height and radius; canonical capsule |
| CapsuleEndpoints | Local endpoints and radius; capsule half-height is half endpoint separation, placed at midpoint with canonical Y aligned to endpoint vector |
| Cylinder / RoundCylinder | Half-height/radius, plus border radius for rounded cylinder; separate cylinder/rounded-cylinder shapes |
| ConvexHull | Finite solid support-point cloud; convex hull shape, not a triangle mesh |
| ConvexParts | Nonempty pre-decomposed point clouds in one collider frame; each part validated and compiled as a separate hull shape |
| TriMesh | Finite vertices and in-range triangle indices; triangle-mesh shape, not automatic convex decomposition |
| Heightfield | Validated field data; heightfield shape |

Convex validation requires at least four points spanning a solid; coplanarity
tolerance is1e-12 of cloud extent. Invalid endpoint/point/mesh/field input returns
an error rather than selecting another shape. A ConvexParts collider has one
stable ColliderHandle but multiple dense shapes: `collider_indices(handle)`
returns all of them, while `collider_index(handle)` succeeds only when exactly
one dense shape exists (None for a multi-shape collider). Resolve these again
after topology edits; do not treat a multi-part collider as one hull.
All dimensions/vertices/local translations use world length units (metres in the
plan fixtures); material density/total mass are `ColliderMass::Density(Real)` or
`Mass(Real)`. Both require finite nonnegative values. Body mass changes through
explicit recomputation, not merely by writing collider density. Geometry/contact/
mass validation and current aggregate execution are separate acceptance items.

These are existing Molla methods, not proposed new backend names. Gearbox can
forward them without embedding USD concepts in Molla. Its trait names were
subsequently audited read-only at revision af6ae06; the precise proposed changes
are in `MOLLA_PRIMITIVES_HANDOFF.md`, without implementing them in that checkout.

| Backend operation | Molla public surface |
|---|---|
| Create tree/world joint | `RigidScene::insert_joint(JointDesc) -> Result<JointHandle>`; `parent: None` is world, not fixed-body conversion |
| Create external rigid/compliant link | `insert_rigid_loop_joint(JointDesc)` or `insert_loop_joint(JointDesc, JointSoftness)`; both return `Result<JointHandle>` |
| Distance authoring/readout | `set_distance_limits(JointHandle, DistanceLimits) -> Result<()>`; `distance_limits(...) -> Result<DistanceLimits>`; `RigidWorld::distance_reading(...) -> Option<&DistanceReading>` |
| Cone authoring/readout | `set_cone_limits(JointHandle, SphericalConeLimits) -> Result<()>`; `cone_limits(...) -> Result<SphericalConeLimits>`; `RigidWorld::cone_reading(...) -> Option<&ConeReading>` |
| Axis control | `set_joint_locked_axes(JointHandle, JointAxes)`; `set_joint_limits(JointHandle, JointAxis, Option<[Real; 2]>)`; `set_joint_motor(JointHandle, JointAxis, JointMotor)`; `set_joint_brake(JointHandle, JointAxis, Real)`; `set_joint_velocity_limit(JointHandle, JointAxis, Option<Real>)`; setters return `Result<()>` |
| Axis/compliance readback | `joint_axis_settings(JointHandle, JointAxis) -> Result<JointAxisSettings>`; `joint_locked_axes(...) -> Result<JointAxes>`; `set_joint_softness(JointHandle, Option<JointSoftness>) -> Result<()>`; `joint_softness(...) -> Result<Option<JointSoftness>>` |
| Authored frames | `set_joint_frames(JointHandle, Transform, Transform) -> Result<()>`; frames are retained in `JointDesc`, independently of traversal direction |
| Material/collision authoring | `ColliderDesc.contact_material`, `.friction`, `.restitution`, `.enabled`, `.memberships`, `.filter`; `insert_collider(ColliderDesc) -> Result<ColliderHandle>` and `replace_collider(ColliderHandle, ColliderDesc) -> Result<()>`; read via `collider(...) -> Option<&ColliderDesc>` |
| Mass authoring | `BodyDesc.additional_mass: Option<MassProperties>`; collider `.mass: ColliderMass`; `set_collider_mass(ColliderHandle, ColliderMass) -> Result<()>`; `RigidWorld::recompute_body_mass(BodyHandle) -> Result<()>`; preserve `MassProperties` full tensor and local COM |
| Explicit pair permissions | `set_body_pair_excluded(BodyHandle, BodyHandle, bool) -> Result<()>` and `set_collider_pair_excluded(ColliderHandle, ColliderHandle, bool) -> Result<()>`; these supplement, not replace, bit masks |
| General load readout | `RigidWorld::set_reaction_readout(bool) -> Result<()>`; `joint_reaction(JointHandle) -> Option<&JointReaction>`; `joint_reaction_samples() -> Option<&[JointReactionSample]>` |
| Break authoring/lifecycle | `RigidScene::set_joint_break_limits(JointHandle, JointBreakLimits) -> Result<()>`; `joint_break_limits(JointHandle) -> Result<JointBreakLimits>`; `joint_broken(JointHandle) -> Result<bool>`; `repair_joint(JointHandle) -> Result<()>`; `RigidWorld::joint_break_events() -> &[JointBreakEvent]`; `drain_joint_break_events() -> Vec<JointBreakEvent>` |
| CPU/GPU world | `RigidWorld::from_scene(RigidScene)` or `from_scene_gpu(RigidScene, Arc<Engine>)`; optional `from_scene_gpu_with_contact_capacity(..., GpuContactCapacity)`; constructors return `Result<RigidWorld>` |

The six minimal runtime examples remain in
`crates/molla-solvers/examples/runtime_primitives.rs`, with commands and lifecycle
documentation in `examples/README.md`. No Gearbox changes were made. Its eventual
adapter must preserve both optional distance/cone fields, the full tensor/COM,
all authored frames, every D6 axis/drive and explicit collision permissions.
Resolve dense indices from stable handles after edits; do not retain them across
topology rebuilds. Negative USD sentinels must be converted to `None`, not passed
as physical Molla bounds. Stage units, collection resolution and scene routing
remain importer responsibilities.

Loads use world axes in N/Nm, with torque about each authored endpoint anchor.
Body force channels instead use COM torque. Missing/stale readout is `None`, not
zero. Break thresholds are inclusive; zero can break on a valid zero-load sample,
and optional positive infinity disables that threshold. Events retain the stable
handle/sample and successful frame/substep timing until explicitly drained;
draining does not repair. Breaking keeps body state and explicit pair exclusions.
Hot softness gains, motors, brakes and body damping activate affected endpoints;
softness toggles and structural limits rebuild. Topology toggles are not hot edits.

Explicit friction requires finite `0 <= mu_dynamic <= mu_static`. If no pair is
authored, the legacy shape coefficient supplies both regimes. Static response
attempts zero contact slip within the static Coulomb disk; sliding uses the
dynamic disk. Mixing follows the per-material combine rule, with priority
Average < Min < Multiply < Max. Rolling speed is not contact slip. Preserve the
specialised tyre/track ownership boundary rather than replacing those laws.

## P0 execution-path audit

### Live CPU runtime

`RigidScene::insert_joint` / mutation -> transactional `runtime::compile` ->
`runtime/tree.rs::compile_joints` -> `ModelBuilder` -> host `Model`, `State`,
`Control` -> `RigidWorld::step` -> sleeping or active CPU collision orchestration
-> articulated Featherstone response -> `RigidScene::commit_step`.

- The compiler re-roots trees, maps stable handles to dense indices, and copies
  compatible generalized state/control across rebuilds. Loop joints are omitted
  from the reduced-coordinate tree and require compliance.
- `RigidWorld::from_scene` explicitly constructs a CPU solver. Each active
  substep refreshes collision geometry, invokes loop/wheel/track/device force
  callbacks, and runs CPU articulated integration and penalty contacts.
- `loop_forces::apply` builds world-anchor wrench rows and uses articulation
  Jacobians and the coupled mass response. Its output is force on the child and
  torque about the child's joint anchor. It is not general tree reaction recovery.
- `commit_step` requires readable, finite host pose, body velocity, body force,
  joint-coordinate and joint-velocity arrays. Device-only output cannot be
  committed directly to today's runtime.

### GPU component route at the initial baseline

`ModelBuilder` -> `Model::upload_to_device` / `State::upload_to_device` /
`Control::upload_to_device` -> `FeatherstoneSolver::new_gpu` ->
`FeatherstoneKernel::dispatch` -> `featherstone.wgsl` -> explicit buffer readback.

- `step_with_collision_response` rejects GPU execution. Swapping the publicly
  accessible `RigidWorld.solver` does not create a GPU runtime route.
- GPU Featherstone rejects compliance, reversed joints and acceleration motors.
  Stable feedback additionally requires rigorous dynamics and scalar drive
  coordinates. These are limitations to resolve, not final conformance claims.
- The kernel currently updates `body_q`, `joint_q`, and `joint_qd`, **not**
  `body_qd`. Body velocity reconstruction is an explicit runtime-bridge dependency.
- Its external body wrenches come from `State::body_f`; the kernel does not bind
  `Control::body_external_f`. Runtime input routing must account for this.
- Multi-substep `FeatherstoneSolver::step` currently uses host scratch operations;
  a GPU-resident runtime needs device ping-pong rather than this host path.
- The kernel retains its pipeline but creates bind groups/uniform buffers and
  performs several separate copy submissions per dispatch. Persistent bindings,
  bounded allocation, batched dispatch and resource-retention gates remain open.
- Articulations are limited to 32 joints by this shader, with failure bit 32 for
  overflow/constraint failures. The bridge must validate limits and consume the
  status buffer instead of publishing unchecked state.
- GPU FEM has a separate `FemRigidGpuSystem` orchestration route. It does not
  consume a live `RigidScene` and is not evidence of the requested rigid runtime.

### Distance characterisation

- Both runtime rejection sites still intentionally reject `Distance` and `Cable`.
- CPU/GPU lower-level distance code projects relative coordinates and removes
  radial velocity. It does not establish coupled endpoint/articulation response.
- The rigorous branch picks a finite min-only or max-only bound even when slack;
  its boundary projection also removes inward motion at a maximum boundary.
  Passing existing fixed-length pendulum tests does not certify interval semantics.
- `loop_forces` currently enumerates six scalar frame coordinates; treating a
  distance link as those locks would incorrectly weld it. A radial row with both
  COM lever arms and coupled response is required before lifting the guards.

## Live GPU runtime bridge

`RigidWorld::from_scene_gpu(scene, Arc<Engine>)` now constructs the GPU backend in
the existing world API. `RigidWorld::step` routes GPU worlds through persistent
device state, not CPU stepping. This is an initial tree-dynamics bridge, **not**
the completed contact/constraint runtime required by the plan.

Execution:

1. Validate supported settings before advancing the scene.
2. Compile/upload a model on `RigidScene::model_stamp` changes. That identity is
   separate from pose/velocity edits; control and gravity edits synchronize without
   recreating the model or pipeline.
3. Upload the current authoritative host state once at the frame boundary and
   synchronize controls/gravity. Run each substep on device, alternating two
   retained state buffers. No substep body-state readback or CPU dynamics solve.
4. Reconstruct both poses and world COM velocities in the GPU integration kernel,
   including parent angular transport, local frames and COM offsets.
5. Read one packed frame buffer containing fault status, body poses/velocities,
   joint coordinates and velocities. Validate and atomically commit the host scene.

The frame-boundary full-state upload/readback is an explicit synchronization and
bandwidth cost of preserving the existing immediate host readout/mutation API.
It is not a compact-event-only production transfer path. GPU reaction/break event
processing must remain on device when those packages are added.

`GpuRuntimeDiagnostics` reports model compilations, actual bind-group creations
for the current model, completed frames, last substep count and state transfer
bytes (model/control uploads are explicitly excluded from the state-byte fields).
The kernel retains its uniform buffer and two alternating binding sets, and
batches its state copies and compute dispatch into one submission per substep.
The runtime retains the readback buffer. Full benchmark/host-allocation attribution
and GPU timestamp measurements remain outstanding.

```rust,no_run
use std::sync::Arc;
use molla_compute::{Backend, Engine};
use molla_sim::runtime::{BodyDesc, RigidScene};
use molla_solvers::rigid_world::RigidWorld;

let engine = Arc::new(Engine::new(Backend::AutoGpu)?);
let mut scene = RigidScene::new()?;
let body = scene.insert_body(BodyDesc::default())?;
let mut world = RigidWorld::from_scene_gpu(scene, engine)?;
world.step(1.0 / 120.0)?;
let velocity = world.scene.body_velocity(body)?;
let diagnostics = world.gpu_diagnostics().unwrap();
# Ok::<(), molla_core::Error>(())
```

### Current explicit GPU runtime restrictions

Colliders/contact response, loop joints, compliant/reversed joints, kinematic
bodies, body damping, acceleration motors, brakes, control-buffer body wrenches,
actuator devices, wheels/tracks, host force callbacks and sleeping are rejected.
`RigidScene::add_body_wrench` uses the supported state-force route. Articulations
above 32 joints are rejected before dispatch. Stable GPU feedback still requires
scalar drive coordinates. These are unfinished plan requirements, not the final
intended supported subset. No CPU fallback is used to mask them.

Shader/pipeline and dispatch validation errors are captured as `Result` errors;
device health and solver fault status are checked before scene publication.
Replacing the world's solver behind the bridge is rejected rather than mixing
devices or a stale articulation layout. Unsupported post-construction edits leave
the last scene state unchanged and can be removed before resuming.

### Bridge regressions and numerical evidence

The first fixed-only scene failed because zero-length generalized buffers had no
device mirrors. Binding them all to a single fallback then exposed a wgpu
read-only/read-write aliasing validation failure. The dispatcher now uses separate
empty writable coordinate/velocity buffers and omits zero-length copies.

The expanded one-second loaded/frame/COM/inertia fixture exposed a **1.416e-3 m**
slider CPU/GPU position mismatch (velocity mismatch 1.833e-3). No tolerance was
relaxed. CPU velocity drives solve against the predicted velocity under all loads;
the GPU previously stabilized only the motor's isolated feedback. GPU feedback now
solves the coupled bounded velocity-drive system through articulated inverse mass.

After that correction, maxima over one second at 1/120 s, eight device substeps:

| Joint | Position error (m) | Rotation error (rad) | Linear/angular velocity error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ball | 6.783e-7 | 1.040e-6 | 2.934e-6 |
| Revolute | 2.723e-6 | 7.015e-7 | 6.370e-6 |
| Prismatic | 3.257e-6 | 7.703e-7 | 6.906e-6 |

Fixtures have floating parents, rotated local frames, offset COMs, full symmetric
inertia tensors, child loads and live scalar velocity-motor edits. Other tests cover
1/2/8 substeps, insertion/deletion, stable handles, gravity and velocity edits,
nonidentity fixed frames, unsupported-feature rollback, empty scenes and invalid dt.

The resource-counter test warms four frames then checks 20 more frames with live
velocity edits. HAL resources stay `[72 buffers, 526528 buffer bytes, 12 groups,
3 pipelines, 3 shader modules]` on this device/run. Explicit creation diagnostics
remain at **one model compilation and 11 solver bind groups** after warm-up.
These numbers include runtime/driver resources and are not a primitive speedup claim.

Final bridge regression results:

- `make test APP_TARGET='-p molla-sim'`: **68 passed**, including one doctest.
- `make test-primitives-baseline`: **56 passed**.
- `make test-primitives-baseline-gpu`: **12 passed** on the actual GPU.
- `make test-primitives-runtime-gpu`: **8 passed**, including retained resources
  and atomic rejection/recovery after a device-detected numerical fault.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `make check APP_TARGET='-p molla-solvers --features resource-counters --all-targets'`:
  passed; the unchanged `featherstone_stop_momentum` test reports an unused
  `common/gpu_readback.rs::body_poses` helper warning.

Logs, initial failures and source/device metadata are in
[`benchmarks/primitives/runtime-gpu-2026-09-28/`](benchmarks/primitives/runtime-gpu-2026-09-28/).
Full workspace verification and the plan's new primitive acceptance gates remain
outstanding. The focused check does not establish a passing strict `harden` gate.


## Repairs and validation

### Scalar equality locks

The original CPU baseline failed
`joint_control::scalar_equality_limits_resist_effort_and_preserve_authored_motor`
with `Solver("scalar stop reaction left an infeasible velocity")`. Equality DOFs
were already removed from the CPU motion subspace and skipped by the unilateral
reaction solver, but integration incorrectly required an ordinary stop reaction.

CPU integration now writes the authored locked coordinate and zero generalized
velocity for the same finite equality predicate used by the motion subspace.
This retains existing equality-lock authoring semantics; changing the equality
target can snap the coordinate. This is **not** a distance/cone projection policy.

GPU scalar motion subspaces now exclude equality-locked DOFs, and integration
clears their velocity. The new regression initially observed `qd=-2.9` from
incoming `qd=-3` under a 10-unit effort at `dt=0.01`, despite the coordinate being
locked. The repaired test covers hinge/slider, incoming velocities -3/0/+3,
nonzero target 0.2, and preserved CPU motor control after unlocking.

A second GPU test checks coupled load transfer: two coincident bodies with unit
mass/inertia, free parent, equality-locked scalar child, 10 N or N m child load,
`dt=0.01`. Parent generalized velocity must be 0.05, relative velocity zero,
and GPU/CPU generalized velocities must agree within 1e-6. It does not claim
general GPU body-velocity readout or live-runtime certification.

### Explicit unsupported GPU contacts

`FeatherstoneKernel::dispatch` previously accepted and ignored nonempty contacts.
It now returns an explicit unsupported contact-response error before changing
device state. The GPU regression checks the error and unchanged output coordinate.
This fail-closed guard must be replaced by the real GPU contact response for P4;
it is not the final requested support level.

tests. Logs are `molla-primitives-after-cpu.log` and
`molla-primitives-after-gpu.log` in the linked baseline directory.
The first coupled-test attempt incorrectly routed the force through the unused
control buffer and read the unwritten body-velocity buffer; it failed the analytic
oracle at zero response. The corrected test uses `State::body_f` and validates
generalized velocities against both CPU and the analytic 0.05 result.

```bash
export NVIDIA_VERSION="$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | head -n 1)"
nix develop --impure -c make test-primitives-baseline
nix develop --impure -c make test-primitives-baseline-gpu
```

These explicitly named **baseline** targets are not the final `test-primitives`
acceptance targets. `check-all`, `test-all`, `harden`, the new physical acceptance

## P1 CPU distance checkpoint — partial, not package acceptance

`RigidScene::insert_joint` now accepts `JointType::Distance` as an external
impulse link. It does not select a child-only reduced-coordinate projection or
merge endpoint trees. `DistanceLimits { min: Option<Real>, max: Option<Real> }`
and `set_distance_limits` author independent finite, nonnegative radial bounds;
invalid edits are atomic. New links default to both bounds disabled. Cable remains
unsupported and separate. Axis drives/locks and compliance are not radial settings.

The active CPU substep constructs COM-wrench anchor Jacobians on both endpoints,
uses each articulation's full mass response, and solves the coupled bounded
impulses by connected island. Scalar hinge/slider stops in the same island enter
the same solve. Corrected generalized velocities are integrated from the substep
input coordinates. No endpoint pose is independently teleported. Redundant rows
use the existing mass pseudoinverse; inconsistent immovable constraints fail
without committing scene state.

Zero minimum alone imposes no restriction. Zero maximum, including a disabled
minimum, uses three bilateral anchor-coincidence rows. Positive minimum at
coincident anchors initially chose world +X deterministically; nonzero separation
uses the radial direction. The endpoint-exchange checkpoint below corrects the
coincident convention on both backends.

`RigidWorld::distance_reading` exposes final separation/violation, the last loaded
bound during the frame, and frame-average world force on the child anchor. Scene
edits and failed step attempts invalidate the cached reading. The first fixture
run passed 4/5 tests but failed with `left: Inactive, right: Maximum`: a later
zero-impulse substep hid an earlier stop impulse. Frame accumulation now retains
the last non-inactive bound. This is not general joint reaction/breakage support.

- closed triangle with a redundant link and conserved linear momentum;
- distance plus scalar stop sharing the articulated response;

## P1 live GPU distance checkpoint — partial, not package acceptance

Runtime-created distance links now execute on the GPU instead of being rejected.
Static topology compiles into connected-island articulation and radial-row tables.
Every substep evaluates GPU CRBA masses and endpoint-anchor Jacobians, factors the
coupled island response, solves impulses, and re-integrates the corrected generalized
velocities with GPU Featherstone drift. No CPU physics fallback or per-substep
state/reaction readback is used. World and fixed endpoints have zero response.

The row solve uses conjugate gradients from zero for bilateral-only systems,
including minimum-norm load sharing for the tested redundant equality links.
Mixed unilateral/scalar-stop systems use projected Gauss-Seidel, with a finite
iteration budget and a complementarity residual check. The device fault status
reports invalid mass factorization with bit 256 and unsatisfied rows with bit 512;
either prevents the frame from committing. General rank-deficient mixed-bound
reaction allocation and conditioning sweeps still need certification.

Both ping-pong states retain CRBA/Jacobian requests, uniforms and bind groups.
The new `MassMatrixDispatch` / `JacobianDispatch` prepared APIs encode into the
caller's command encoder; legacy dispatch callers retain their existing API.
Radial rows record frame-average child-anchor force and an integer last-active
substep tag. Only those diagnostics join the existing frame-boundary state/status
readback. Separation/violation are computed from the committed-frame candidate.
Disabled and fully unbounded links perform no radial solve.

- a distance link coupled to an articulated scalar stop;
- zero maximum, fixed-only infeasibility, atomic failure and corrected-input resume;
- live bounds/removal mutations and warm GPU resource retention;
- ten-second pendulum runs at three timesteps, with one-second CPU trajectory gates.

## P1 sleeping and kinematic boundaries — integrated, broader gates still open

The temporary CPU distance/sleep and GPU sleep/kinematic rejections are removed.
CPU active-articulation stepping now calls radial constraints after each selected
substep, and selective drift retains sleeping coordinates, poses and velocities.
The same dependency/wake closure selects whole islands on both backends. GPU
Featherstone and radial kernels have retained activation buffers; inactive islands
skip dynamics and constraint solving rather than being advanced and then restored.
GPU stepping preserves automatic quiet-window accounting and acknowledges existing
sleepers only after successful frame commit. Wholly sleeping links publish no new
reaction sample, rather than an invented zero reaction.

Explicit sleep, automatic sleep, independent active groups, non-waking velocity
edits, fixed-boundary wake, and endpoint edits are covered on CPU and GPU.
Distance-bound changes now wake endpoint dependencies without waking unrelated
sleepers; invalid and unchanged settings retain the existing atomic/no-op contract.

GPU Featherstone now binds body flags, preserves fixed/kinematic input poses, and
retains prescribed kinematic COM velocities. This also prevents a moved fixed
boundary being reset to its original compiled joint frame. Kinematic bodies are
prescribed inputs, as on CPU: callers author their pose and velocity; the solver
does not autonomously integrate the kinematic pose. Radial row rates include
prescribed endpoint anchor velocities plus the solved generalized-velocity change,
including angular lever arms. Moving boundaries prevent dependent islands sleeping.

The one-second moving-boundary fixture translates at 0.2 m/s and rotates at
0.15 rad/s, with an offset anchor, 1/120-second frames and eight substeps. It retains
an unrelated sleeping island and requires only one GPU model compilation across
120 authored pose updates. Position errors were:

|---|---:|---:|
| 0 N | 1.805780e-6 | 5.373305e-5 |
| 8 N | 3.343419e-7 | 5.168843e-5 |

The loaded run passed a strict 1% per-frame CPU/GPU reaction gate (with a 1 N
reference floor), and both runs matched their actual per-frame momentum balance
within 1e-5 N s and cumulative CPU/GPU impulse within 1e-3 N s.

**Precision observation, not hidden by a tolerance change:** the first unloaded
run failed an additional 0.01 N instantaneous near-zero-force comparison at frame

run, peak force difference reached 0.0278725 N despite position error below 2e-6 m.
The small-substep f32 reaction jitter remains documented; instantaneous unloaded

It does not claim the original extra near-zero-force assertion passed. First failure
and diagnostic logs remain in the checkpoint directory. The first CPU fixture also

## P1 endpoint exchange, mutation and physical scale sweep

The new public-runtime exchange test exposed a CPU/GPU defect at coincident
anchors with a positive radial bound. Reversing the link's endpoints reversed
both bodies' physical motion: the first frame differed by 4.8 m on CPU and
4.7999997 m on GPU, with opposite velocities of approximately 288 m/s. This
fixture starts one metre outside its admissible minimum and deliberately exercises
the undefined-normal case. The previous unconditional +X fallback was not
antisymmetric under endpoint exchange.

Both paths now use world X oriented from the lower stable body handle to the
higher; a world parent uses positive X. Reversing the endpoints therefore reverses
the row direction and reported child force without changing either physical body
response. The compiled GPU row stores this orientation in the unused parent-anchor
w component, with no new allocation, binding or per-frame upload. This convention
is documented on `DistanceLimits` and is independent of dense compaction indices.

`runtime_distance_contract.rs` adds shared CPU/GPU fixtures:

- Ten one-second endpoint-exchange cases: positive minimum/equality from coincident
  anchors, zero coincidence, free zero minimum, outside minimum/maximum, tangential
  equality, interval activation, unbounded motion, and rotated offset anchors with
  non-diagonal inertia and COM offsets. They check body trajectories/velocities,
  opposite child reaction impulses, activation, length and free-system momentum.
- A live mutation sequence checks unrelated-body compaction, disabled/re-enabled
  links and bodies, authored frame/bound edits, no-bound motion, link deletion and
  replacement, endpoint-cascade removal, stale-handle rejection, readout invalidation,
  rejected-edit atomicity, and an unrelated motor's settings and physical response.
  Wrenches persist between frames; this fixture explicitly resets each authored
  force before adding its next 10 N load.
- Forty fixed/free two-body scale cases at each of 1/60, 1/120 and 1/240-second
  frames, eight substeps, ten seconds per case. Lengths are 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 m;
  mass pairs are (0.1,0.1), (1,1), (100,100), (1,1000) and (1000,1) kg. Inertia
  scales as mass times length squared. Free rotation is checked independently.
  The free pair has a known constant acceleration; the fixed-parent pair has an
  analytic stationary reaction. Gates are 1e-3 relative length, 1e-3 m/rad
  one-second analytic pose error, 1% reaction error with no settling grace, and
  relative momentum errors 1e-6 CPU/1e-3 GPU with a 1e-3 kg m/s reference floor.

The initial complete scale sweeps passed unchanged thresholds. Largest errors:

| Measurement | CPU | GPU |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ten-second relative length | 4.683754e-15 | 2.026558e-6 |
| One-second analytic position, m | 3.730349e-14 | 3.607009e-5 |
| Quasi-static relative reaction | 4.440892e-16 | 1.639128e-7 |

These are aligned, collider-free fixtures, not certification of contact coupling,
mixed redundant-bound reactions, tiny-load instantaneous precision, arbitrary
large-coordinate conditioning or performance. The stationary scale reactions do
not erase the previously recorded moving-boundary force jitter. Both named
distance Make targets include this new contract suite.

**CPU momentum failure at this checkpoint (resolved below):** expanding the exchange fixture to initially rotating
bodies with offset COM and non-diagonal inertia exposed a separate integration
failure. Case 9's first 1/120-second frame (four substeps) had momentum error
9.998740e-6 kg m/s against the unchanged 1e-6 gate. An added public-runtime
single-free-body test reproduces drift without any distance joint: mass 2 kg,
COM `(0.1,-0.2,0.05)` m, initial angular velocity `(0.1,-0.2,0.3)` rad/s and
the same non-diagonal inertia yield peak error 1.441090e-5 kg m/s over one second.
Both CPU regressions remained enabled and failing; the CPU distance target was
**not green**. No tolerance was relaxed or extra substeps substituted. The
unconstrained reproduction isolates this from endpoint-exchange row orientation;
free-body coordinate/COM transport through integration needs further investigation.
GPU passes all ten exchange cases at its separate 1e-3 momentum gate, which does
not certify the stronger CPU requirement.

`make check-all` passed across the workspace/all targets, with the existing unused
`body_poses` test-helper warning. The CPU primitive baseline passed **56 tests**.
These checks do not override the two new numerical failures.

The GPU regression passed the six existing distance tests and three sleep tests;

The strengthened mutation rotation assertion initially compared a raw quaternion
dot product to unity, conflating small f32 norm error with orientation change.

## P1 rotating offset COM — implicit-root coordinates corrected

Runtime-created implicit free roots now place their child frame at the root body's
COM, rather than its origin. Their world translation coordinates/rates are therefore
COM position/velocity; the body origin is reconstructed through the existing child
frame transform. This removes the rotating lever arm from the root's linear
coordinate integration and radial impulse redrift. Both backends consume the same
compiled model: no post-step momentum projection, extra substeps, CPU fallback or
new device dispatch is used. Explicitly authored joint frames are unchanged.

A COM edit changes the implicit frame. The compiler retains control buffers but
reseeds coordinates/rates from the preserved body pose and velocity field rather
than copying obsolete origin-based coordinates. This is an intentional correction
to the implicit generalized-coordinate convention, documented on `RigidScene`.
Two simulation tests that previously demanded bit-identical generalized coordinates
across COM edits now check the shifted COM coordinates/rates and unchanged physical
pose, velocity field, world wrench application and wake behaviour. Their former
failure is retained in `sim-first.log`; physical checks were not removed.

Both previously failing CPU tests pass at their original four substeps and 1e-6
momentum gate, including the rotating off-centre distance exchange fixture. For the
one-second free-body reproduction, peak linear momentum error is now
7.850462e-17 kg m/s on CPU (previously 1.441090e-5), and 3.039252e-8 on GPU.

The new `runtime_com_roots.rs` CPU/GPU fixture repeatedly moves the COM and changes
mass, compacts an unrelated body, and checks exact body-pose preservation, velocity
at a world point, root coordinate/rate reseeding and world wrench preservation.
After each edit it applies a known force to the spinning body for one second and
checks linear momentum against the analytic impulse. Both backends passed. The
simulation package passed **68 tests**, and the CPU primitive baseline **56**.
The shared distance contract now also runs the free-body momentum reproduction on
GPU, and the named distance Make targets include the new COM-edit tests.

The first full GPU regression then exposed reaction roundoff in the existing
rotating offset/redundant-link fixture: CPU child force was approximately
`(-0.0560363,0.0176828,0.00724884)` N versus GPU
`(-0.0436030,0.0137622,0.00563690)` N, exceeding its unchanged per-frame gate.
GPU radial geometry now evaluates eligible COM-root anchors directly from root
translation coordinates plus the rotated local anchor-to-COM offset. It avoids
reconstructing an origin and then adding another rotated offset. Compiled endpoint
metadata carries the root coordinate index; other endpoints retain their existing
pose-based path. This adds 32 bytes per row, with no new dispatch or binding.
The targeted offset/redundant-link rerun passed, with one-second CPU/GPU peak
position difference 6.030304e-7 m. The first failure is retained; no reaction
tolerance was changed.

The complete named CPU distance target passed **19 tests**. A workspace
`make test-all` build completed all targets, then stopped at a sensor GPU benchmark
because the unwrapped command could not find an adapter. The subsequent full
workspace run uses `NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c nixVulkan
make test-all`; this is an environment correction, not a passing workspace result.

Final named distance lanes passed **19 CPU and 14 GPU tests**, including the
original reaction gate and new rotating-COM/mass-edit fixtures. Warm GPU distance
resources remained stable at 91 buffers, 529680 buffer bytes, 28 bind groups,
6 pipelines and 6 shaders. The additional 32 bytes in that single-row fixture
are compiled anchor metadata. Source fingerprints and a clean `git diff --check`

This does not certify angular-momentum conservation or arbitrary explicitly framed

```
crates/molla-geometry/src/lbvh.rs:608:25
lbvh::redispatch: NaN AABB centroid (NaN,NaN,NaN)
```

The same failure reproduced with
`nix develop --impure -c nixVulkan make test APP_TARGET='-p molla-geometry --features gpu --bench bench_broadphase_pairs'`.
The original workspace log and focused `broadphase-bench-repro.log` are retained
under the COM-root checkpoint. The refit centroid check narrows bounds to f32

code and does not certify it.

### Implemented geometry and configuration only

[`MOLLA_CONE_GEOMETRY.md`](MOLLA_CONE_GEOMETRY.md) defines the disk-log ellipse,
cyclic axis convention, analytic angular Jacobian, zero/disabled extents,
violation units, GPU representation and explicit current singularity restriction.
It was written before implementing the evaluator. This ellipse is a Molla design
choice, not an assertion that OpenUSD mandates this numerical construction.

- `SphericalConeLimits` validates independent optional half-angles in `[0,pi]`.
  The CPU evaluator produces bilateral zero-extent rows and one scaled elliptical
  unilateral row for positive extents. Circular cones reduce to primary-axis
  angular separation; child twist and quaternion sign do not change the geometry.
- `ConeGeometryKernel` evaluates the same geometry in standalone GPU batches.
  Requests/results each occupy 80 bytes; bindings are prepared once and reused.
  Status distinguishes valid, unsupported antipodal, and invalid geometry.
  Unrepresentable positive extents are rejected rather than converted to locks.
- `RigidScene::{cone_limits,set_cone_limits,cone_joints}` supplies sparse,
  validated tree/loop ball-joint configuration. Mutations preserve handles,
  distinguish no-ops, activate endpoint dependencies, and clean up on deletion.
- `RigidWorld` rejects active bounded cones before construction/stepping on both
  backends until the coupled solver consumes them. Rejection preserves state,
  pending wrenches and callbacks. Disabled joints/bodies and unrestricted extents
  do not trigger this cone-specific guard; other GPU restrictions remain.

The first GPU run exposed the WGSL reserved identifier `meta`; the shader member
was renamed to `info` without changing the packed layout. The next run exposed a
non-cardinal near-antipodal Jacobian error: GPU `-0.35068366` versus CPU
`3.920031859e-9` at `pi-0.001`. This was not fixed by relaxing the original gates.
Packing the quaternion in the orthonormal cone basis before f32 narrowing and
using radial/azimuthal derivative forms removed that cancellation in the tested
component route. The circular-cone azimuthal term now cancels algebraically.
Future device-only frame transformations still need their own precision gates.

row disagreement was `6.606505e-4`. Gates were `2e-5` ordinarily and `1e-3` at
`pi-0.001`, selected before observing the failed comparison. CPU Jacobians also
passed central finite-difference checks. The final GPU matrix expanded to
**6300 cases** with wide, pi and highly asymmetric extents; all passed three
identical dispatches with the retained bindings. Peak swing/violation disagreement
was `4.579253e-7` radians, with the same peak scaled row disagreement.
The full `molla-sim` lane passed **75 tests including its doctest**. All-target GPU
checks for `molla-sim`, `molla-kernels` and `molla-solvers` passed; an existing

## Initial coupled cone runtime — partial physical acceptance

The standalone geometry is now connected to live runtime stepping, rather than
leaving all bounded cones behind the earlier capability guard. CPU and GPU
assemble cone angular rows with distance rows and scalar stops in the same
articulated-island response. Normalized angular Jacobians apply equal/opposite
torques; corrected velocities are integrated again from the substep input, not
applied as a one-body pose teleport. Zero extents use bilateral impulses and
positive extents use inward-only impulses. Runtime sleep selection is shared.

`RigidWorld::cone_reading(JointHandle)` exposes final swing, angular violation,
frame activation, frame-average child torque in world coordinates, and sample
duration. Readings invalidate on scene mutation and failed steps. This is only
the cone contribution, not the complete P3 joint wrench. Geometry is evaluated
on device within GPU substeps, with retained buffers/bindings and no host solve
or per-substep state readback. The unified GPU row grew from 112 to 176 bytes;
the existing single-distance-row warm test retains 91 buffers, 529744 buffer
bytes, 28 groups, 6 pipelines and 6 shaders. The additional 64 bytes are inline
cone basis/settings fields; no extra per-substep dispatch was added for distance.

CPU additionally executes angular cones on existing compliant external ball
joints. GPU external/loop ball joints and GPU colliders remain explicitly
unsupported. CPU contact and external-loop forces still precede the impulse
projection; they are not solved simultaneously with cone rows in a full contact
complementarity system. The antipodal restriction remains explicit, with input
checks before callbacks/actuator updates and atomic failure/readout invalidation.

### Physical evidence and first failures

- The CPU cone target passed 17 tests: five geometry, two configuration, one
  unsupported-chart atomicity and nine runtime tests. Runtime coverage includes
  loaded circular/elliptical/zero cones on cardinal and arbitrary axes with
  rotated frames, diagonal loaded free twist, two-body angular impulse/reaction,
  cone-plus-radial offset articulation response, mutation/sleep/compaction and a
  gravity-loaded pendulum for ten seconds at 1/60, 1/120 and 1/240 seconds.
- CPU loaded-stop peak violation was `1.909588e-7` radians. Pendulum energy stayed
  within its unchanged 1% gate at every step; initial energy was 5.595546871,
  peak at the coarsest step was 5.600633472, and final energy was about 0.775.
- The CPU external-ball test ran for ten seconds under gravity and applied
  torque, with authored frequency 80 and damping ratio 1. Peak anchor deviation
  was `5.504978e-3` metres, below its 1 cm compliance gate; cone violation was zero.
  This is not a rigid-loop or GPU-loop certification.
- The first GPU loaded-stop run failed its unchanged reaction gate at a rotated
  zero-extent stop: expected 3 Nm cancellation, observed 2.993439436 Nm. Eligible
  tree ball cones now read their relative quaternion from generalized joint
  coordinates instead of subtracting reconstructed world rotations. The full
  16-case loaded-stop matrix then passed; its largest printed final torque error
  was `1.496555e-6` Nm. The angular-momentum, free-axis zero-cone, and all three
  ten-second pendulum cases also passed on GPU. The GPU pendulum's largest
  reported violation was `4.213683e-8` radians.
- GPU mutation/sleep/compaction and unsupported-chart atomicity tests passed.

**Still failing:** `gpu_diagonal_ellipse_retains_loaded_free_twist`. With diagonal
elliptical loading and initial free twist, the angular-velocity vector departs
from its analytic value by `2.051905e-4` rad/s, exceeding the existing `2e-4`
gate. First diagnostic sample: actual `(1.534266472,0.521102726,1.172176003)`;
expected `(1.534287913,0.521055329,1.172374490)`. A two-ULP positional-bias
deadband did not fix it (`2.178476e-4` error) and was reverted. The same fixture
on CPU with f32-quantized initial poses, rates, wrenches and cone bounds passes
the GPU gate; initial parameter quantization alone does not explain the failure.
The defect needs substep rounding/integration/constraint-response diagnosis,
not a tolerance increase. The first failing test remains enabled in the GPU
cone target. No full GPU cone or P2 acceptance is claimed.

Named entry points are `make test-primitives-cone-cpu` and
`make test-primitives-cone-gpu`; existing geometry-only targets remain available.
Evidence and failed experiments are retained under
[`benchmarks/primitives/cone-runtime-2026-09-28/`](benchmarks/primitives/cone-runtime-2026-09-28/).
Final focused regressions passed **19 CPU distance tests, 14 GPU distance tests,
and 56 CPU primitive baselines**. The mixed cone-plus-radial offset articulation

All-target GPU checks for the three affected crates, focused formatting checks

## GPU loaded-twist precision correction

A focused substep probe separated initial input quantization, force projection,
and pose integration. Holding the projection normal fixed produced no drift in
the sampled f32 case. With evolving cone geometry, rounded predicted-velocity
projection produced `1.500735e-4` rad/s error with f64 quaternion integration and
`1.739845e-4` with f32 quaternion integration over 1920 substeps. Combining force
and constraint increments before updating velocity reduced those probe errors to
`2.743761e-6` and `7.261191e-5`, respectively. The latter two now have explicit
numerical regression gates, separate from the live GPU acceptance test.

The GPU Featherstone predictor now retains its per-DOF velocity increment in one
device buffer. The coupled row solver uses that increment directly in row rates
and combines it with the impulse response before adding the net change to the
input velocity. Damping is included; coordinate locks, caps and post-integration
overrides fall back to their actual velocity difference. Drift-only integration
does not overwrite predictor increments. This adds no host solve, substep
readback or new compute dispatch. Resource changes are measured below.

The original `gpu_diagonal_ellipse_retains_loaded_free_twist` test now passes
with its unchanged `2e-4` rad/s velocity gate and unchanged boundary/mean-torque
gates. No positional-bias deadband was reinstated. Broader GPU regressions and
final numerical values are now recorded by the completed named runs:

- Diagonal loaded twist: peak angular-velocity error `1.545427e-4` rad/s,
  boundary error `5.089652e-7`, mean torque error `1.063409e-5` N·m.
- `test-primitives-cone-cpu`: 19 passed; `test-primitives-cone-gpu`: 10 passed,
  including the 6300-case standalone geometry batch and seven live runtime tests.
- Distance regressions: 19 CPU and 14 GPU tests passed. The moving-kinematic
  reaction jitter remains: peak errors `0.0278725` N unloaded and `0.0295956` N
  under the sampled 8 N load. Passing the current fixture does not close that gap.
- Primitive baselines: 56 CPU and 13 GPU tests passed. A new direct kernel test
  verifies retention of a `1e-8` velocity increment even when predicted velocity
  rounds back to `1.0`, plus damping, caps, equality locks and drift preservation.
- GPU runtime contract: 9 passed. Warm distance counters are
  `[92 buffers, 529792 bytes, 28 groups, 6 pipelines, 6 shaders]`; the predictor
  adds one buffer and 48 bytes for this fixture, with no additional groups,
  pipelines or shaders. Warm unconstrained runtime counters are
  `[74, 526576, 12, 3, 3]`; retention assertions passed.
- `make check-all` passed, with the existing unused `body_poses` helper warning
  in `featherstone_stop_momentum`.

## Rigid external ball constraints

`RigidScene::insert_rigid_loop_joint` now accepts ball joints as rigid external
constraints without merging endpoint trees. The existing `insert_loop_joint`
retains its explicit compliance. Ball loops can switch between those modes with
`set_joint_softness`, preserving pose and velocity during the edit; unsupported
scalar controls prevent a transition to rigid mode transactionally. Rigid ball
loops currently reject axis motors, brakes and scalar angular limits rather than
silently ignoring them; use the separate cone configuration for supported limits.

Both CPU and GPU assembly reuse the three anchor-coincidence rows of a zero-radius
constraint, coupled to cone and scalar-stop rows in the same articulated response
solve. Each GPU sample now carries a host-side row-kind discriminator so anchor
force and cone torque belonging to one ball joint are accumulated separately.
`RigidWorld::ball_anchor_reading` returns frame-average world child-anchor force,
separation and sample duration; `cone_reading` remains its separate angular stop
contribution. This is not yet P3's complete general joint reaction API.

CPU results: four live rigid-loop tests, three existing compliant-loop
tests and three cone configuration tests pass. A rotated-frame/full-inertia static
fixture gives anchor error `8.76e-16` m and analytic force/torque errors below

requires cone activation and checks energy growth. At 1/60, 1/120 and 1/240 s its
peak anchor errors are `1.838e-5`, `4.739e-6`, `1.203e-6` m, with zero sampled cone
violation. Initial energy is `7.706898` J; sampled peak is at most `7.707477` J.
A two-articulation impulse fixture preserves linear/angular momentum and
independently free twist with a `1e-8` CPU gate, then checks compaction and shared
sleep/wake. A moving closed-chain fixture couples the external anchor back into
an existing single articulation while its cone is active.

The first GPU batch passed all five tests, including retained resources

`3.44e-6` N·m. Closed-chain one-second CPU/GPU peak differences were `4.80e-6` m
and `9.08e-4` rad; the latter is close to the unchanged `1e-3` rad gate and needs

solved generalized velocity increments at the input force-evaluation pose. It
accounts for applied COM loads, acted contacts and external radial/rigid-ball/
compliant loop loads without double-counting the latter. Reversed tree joints

including non-waking force/motor changes and raw mutable state/control access,
without changing model recompilation or activation semantics. Its overflow path
renews the identity rather than aliasing an old counter value.

## Kinematic reaction support and boundary acceleration correction

Removed the blanket CPU kinematic-readout refusal. CPU RNEA now uses prescribed
world COM/angular velocity and the corresponding zero-COM-acceleration spatial
term. For a fixed recursion origin, that term is `-omega cross v_COM`, not zero.
The same omission existed in CPU and GPU Featherstone's kinematic acceleration
boundary. A new analytic fixture first reproduced a spurious hinge rate of
`-0.002 rad/s` after `0.001 s` with a translating/rotating parent; the CPU/GPU
boundary correction removes it without integrating or altering prescribed poses.

The named CPU reaction target now passes 33 tests. Four new CPU tests cover
fixed/hinge/ball centripetal support, full-inertia gyroscopic torque plus external
loads, reversed authored endpoints, translated/rotated frames and 1/4/8 substeps. The new GPU hinge oracle passes
twenty steps in two translated frames with an unchanged `2e-5 rad/s` rate bound.
The CPU hinge oracle uses `1e-10 rad/s`. Primitive CPU baseline plus distance lanes
pass 75 tests. `check-all` passes with the existing unused test-helper warning.

Kinematic poses remain caller-authored and held during a step. Prescribed COM and
angular velocities are piecewise constant; nonzero prescribed acceleration is not
currently an input. No acceleration or impulse is invented from unrelated pose
edits. An explicit acceleration surface and its GPU parity remain open for
arbitrary accelerating trajectories. General GPU reaction readout is still absent.
The legacy scalar GPU RNEA wrapper rejects prescribed motion it cannot represent;
all four host-side capability tests pass.

Logs: `kinematic-before.log`, `kinematic-after.log`, `kinematic-cpu.log`,
`kinematic-gpu.log`, `kinematic-baselines.log`, `kinematic-capability.log` and
`kinematic-check-all.log` under `benchmarks/primitives/reactions-2026-09-28/`.

## P3b configuration and explicit detachment checkpoint

`JointBreakLimits` and `JointBreakTrigger` now define independent inclusive
force/torque channels. Zero reaches the threshold on any valid sample, including
zero load; `None` and positive infinity disable a channel. Negative/NaN values
and invalid sample magnitudes are rejected. Stable-handle threshold edits touch
dynamics validity and endpoint activation without rebuilding the model.

`RigidScene::break_joints` atomically detaches a deduplicated batch while retaining
descriptors/handles and current body poses/velocities. Broken state persists until
explicit repair/re-enable. Newly free components receive free roots; breaking a
loop leaves its endpoint trees intact. Broken tree edges also release authored
connectivity/world-anchor reservations, allowing replacement edges; conflicting
repair fails atomically. Subsequent state/structure edits no longer propagate
through broken edges, and unrelated sleeping components remain asleep.

Explicit body-pair and collider-pair exclusions now use stable unordered sets and
compile to exact shape pairs, including compound colliders and newly added body
shapes. Breaking a joint removes only that joint's collision restriction. Separate
explicit pair filters and `step_filtered` callbacks still suppress actual contacts.
Deletion/compaction prune or remap the independent policies. GPU capability checks
ignore stored broken/disabled loop metadata but still reject unsupported active
compliant loops after explicit repair.

At this foundation checkpoint, automatic threshold execution and events were not
implemented. Active finite thresholds made stepping fail explicitly without
advancing. The next required work was substep
early-stop/continuation on CPU and GPU, device threshold detection, simultaneous
trigger collection, one-event transactions and full frame rollback. Frame-end
mean comparisons or delayed detachment are not substitutes. Detailed contracts,
current capabilities and integration constraints are in `MOLLA_BREAKAGE.md`.

Validation in `benchmarks/primitives/breakage-2026-09-28/`:

- Eight configuration/topology/policy tests and four live CPU detachment/capability
  tests pass; four GPU detachment/capability tests pass. The motion fixture covers
  fixed, hinge, slider, ball, D6, Free, radial and external-ball joints.
- CPU reaction regressions: 34 pass. Existing primitive baseline/distance lanes:
  75 pass. `cpu-regressions.log` contains those plus the initial six configuration
  tests; the final eight configuration tests are in `sim-regressions.log`.
- All 83 `molla-sim` unit/integration tests and its doctest pass. The ten live GPU
  runtime contract tests pass alongside the four new GPU cases.
- `check-all` passes with the existing unused `body_poses` helper warning. No full
  workspace test or performance certification is claimed; the earlier synchronized
  Featherstone benchmark stall remains open.

## P3b automatic CPU execution checkpoint

The CPU runtime now evaluates inclusive force/torque limits on each actual solved
substep, batches simultaneous triggers, detaches before the next substep and
continues the remaining frame. Sleeping owners are not sampled. Thresholds work
without enabling public reaction diagnostics; below-threshold frames retain the
compiled model. Events contain stable handles, limits, triggering samples and a
zero-based successful outer-step index. Failed calls do not advance that index;
events remain queued until explicitly drained, with a new episode after repair.

A solver-only host checkpoint protects frames without a break. The first break
forks the completed boundary state and retains the exact original scene. Later
failure restores topology, poses/velocities, validity stamps and sleep/settling
state, and discards provisional events. Checkpoints reject both changed model
identity and intervening dynamics-input edits; solver commits alone remain
restorable. External force-callback side effects are outside the transaction.

Contact samples preserve their actual durations. Reaction and legacy loop means
use the full outer-frame duration. Drive/brake means use stable body/joint/local
DOF keys, then remap to the final model so newly free root coordinates cannot
shift another joint's diagnostics. Joint collision restrictions disappear at the
break boundary while independent user exclusions remain effective.
