## P3b device detection and GPU continuation checkpoint

The live GPU runtime now detects limits on instantaneous device reaction samples,
atomically compacts triggering records and publishes its successful halt bit in a
separate ordered pass. All owners finish the same boundary before later queued
substeps stop. The existing ping-pong state copies propagate that boundary without
drifting it again; the host detaches the complete stable-handle batch and resumes
the remaining substeps on newly compiled topology. No CPU solve or per-substep
body-state readback is used for threshold evaluation.

Every threshold-enabled segment reads a 12-byte status/boundary/count notification.
Only triggered records are copied (`112 * count` bytes), alongside boundary state.
Public diagnostics additionally read their usual mean/sample data; when disabled,
full sample-history buffers are not allocated or transferred. The nonbreaking
one-body fixed fixture reads 80 bytes per frame, independent of substeps. Warm
resource retention is tested, but this is not the full performance matrix.

The CPU checkpoint/lazy-fork mechanism also rolls back GPU topology/state after a
later segment fails. Events and frame counters are committed only once per outer
frame. Device-computed segment means are weighted into full-frame means; event
and sample indices remain relative to the original frame. GPU positive finite
thresholds outside normal f32 representation fail explicitly. Inclusive device
comparisons use no artificial epsilon; threshold-tie limitations and measured
fixture load tolerances are documented in `MOLLA_BREAKAGE.md`.

Seven automatic GPU fixtures exercise substeps 1/4/8, diagnostics on/off, analytic
post-break free motion, simultaneous independent channels and CPU parity, explicit
repair, sleeping zero limits, delayed angular-stop peaks at two successive break
boundaries, a 130-owner batch spanning workgroups, fixed/hinge/slider/ball/D6 and
radial/external-ball joints, and rollback when newly free motion overflows. The
overflow test verifies the original model/dynamics/activation identities and no
provisional events, then successfully retries. Initial evidence is in
`benchmarks/primitives/breakage-2026-09-28/automatic-gpu.log`; final expanded
regressions are recorded in `automatic-gpu-full-regressions.log`.
That serialized invocation passes **36 GPU test executions**: four explicit
detachment/capability tests, seven automatic-break fixtures, fifteen general/live/
kinematic/legacy reaction tests and ten live runtime contract tests.

The companion CPU breakage/reaction lanes pass 59 test executions, and workspace
`make check-all` passes with the existing unused `body_poses` helper warning.
Those logs are `gpu-break-cpu-regressions.log` and `gpu-break-check-all.log` in
the same directory. Source formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

With the added break buffers, the warm opt-in fixed-support reaction fixture
retains `[75 buffers, 528432 bytes, 19 groups, 7 pipelines, 5 shaders]`; its 1044-byte
frame readback is unchanged when no finite threshold is configured. The moving
floating-chain reaction regression retains its `1.5672723e-4` peak absolute wrench
error. These are bounded regression observations, not workload certification.

This does not close P3b: broad scale/moving-chain/mixed-scene and performance gates,
registered actuator transactions, GPU contact/compliance/control capability gaps
and the earlier full-workspace Featherstone benchmark stall remain open.

## P4 coefficient route and CPU static/dynamic contact checkpoint

`ContactMaterial::friction` now accepts an optional `FrictionCoefficients` pair.
Legacy shape/collider coefficients resolve to equal static/dynamic values. Finite
nonnegative coefficients with `mu_dynamic <= mu_static` are required; reversed
pairs and pair-combination overflow fail explicitly. The existing material pair
rule is applied separately to both channels. Generated `Contacts` carry both
values through capacity growth/reduction; static metadata also survives the
actual GPU narrow-phase route. This is not GPU friction solving.

CPU Featherstone retains its normal penalty predictor but replaces its tangential
viscous force with a coupled articulated impulse solve before coordinate redrift.
Contact groups use full tangential Jacobian/mass Gram responses and circular
Coulomb disks. Feasible static solutions use a spectral solve; bounded block
updates and an interior-point fallback cover redundant/near-redundant manifolds.
The fallback was needed because independent block updates stalled on physically
almost redundant support points, not because the physical displacement gate was
relaxed. There is no persistent tangential spring/warm-start cache.

The explicit capture band is `1e-4 m/s`; solved disk KKT residuals must be at most
`1e-7 m/s`. Static trials that exceed the capture band transition to dynamic
friction. The old stiffness/smoothing fields remain available to the standalone
legacy penalty evaluator and are not reinterpreted. Contact diagnostics report
regime, disk coefficient and actual tangential impulse/force. The tracked-vehicle
path clears both coefficients when its own traction solve owns the contact.

Measured five-second, nonsleeping holding tests now pass with real collision
manifolds. The cuboid block's peak tangential displacement is `2.360e-5 m`; a
four-pad compound block reaches `3.687e-5 m`. The translated/rotated compound
fixture's post-settling four-second drift is `1.061e-7 m`. Bounds remain `2e-4 m`
total displacement and `1e-6 m` post-settling drift. The controlled kinetic fixture
measures `3.039090262261243 m/s^2` against analytic `3.0390902622612845 m/s^2`.
The fixture normal stiffness is `1e5 N/m`; an exploratory `1e4 N/m` case showed
`3.69e-4 m` initial elastic deflection and was not claimed to pass the tighter gate.

Eight live runtime tests also cover stop/re-stick, force reversal, conveyors,
zero/equal legacy coefficients, invalid material-edit atomicity, separation and
deletion, collider-endpoint exchange/compaction, and sleep/surface-edit wake.
The disk-level check covers bounds and fixed-predictor slip-energy dissipation;
the ten simplified tracked-vehicle tests remain passing. Details, numerical
policy, limitations and evidence routes are in `MOLLA_FRICTION.md` and
`benchmarks/primitives/friction-2026-09-28/`.

The combined CPU friction/baseline/reaction/breakage invocation passes **151 test
executions** and `make check-all` (existing unused test-helper warning only).
`cpu-full.log` records that run. The actual GPU narrow-phase material route passes
its one test with zero CPU narrow-phase calls (`gpu-material-route.log`); this
checks coefficient transport, not device contact physics. Targeted formatting and
`git diff --check` pass. No dependencies, branches or commits were changed.
The full default-feature `molla-solvers --lib` invocation also passes 87 tests,
with three explicitly ignored CPU benchmarks; this does not include the stalled
all-target Featherstone GPU benchmark.

GPU contact response/friction, joint-stop/external-loop coupling, broad scales,
energy/restitution and resource/performance gates remain open. P4 is not complete;
the previous full-workspace Featherstone benchmark stall remains unresolved.

## P4 GPU broad-phase residency prerequisite

The initial contact-path audit found that `LbvhBroadPhase::dispatch_no_readback`
called the synchronous host-returning `dispatch`, while `refit_in_place` also
downloaded the header and pair arrays. Neither was a device-only substep path.
Both now submit without mapping, polling or collecting pairs. Full builds still
compute/upload host AABBs and Morton codes and dispatch the existing radix sort;
only refitting is currently suitable for the retained substep path.

`encode_refit` appends refit and pair generation to a caller-owned encoder, with
no resource construction, uploads, submissions or readback. Its three retained
LBVH bind groups are rebuilt only when backing buffers change. Refits preserve
the root in device `pair_count[1]` while clearing the emitted count in command
order. This supports many AABB producer/refit/consumer sequences in one submission
without queue writes resetting later substeps early. A missing or count-mismatched
topology is rejected. Single-leaf trees now initialize/refit their leaf correctly;
empty builds clear the header and invalidate cached topology rather than exposing
stale pairs. Node-layout documentation now states the actual 48-byte stride.

The resident path never grows pair buffers based on a hidden readback. The device
count is a high-water mark; consumers must check overflow and read at most the
allocated capacity. Host-returning APIs retain their existing truncated-result
plus next-dispatch-growth behavior. The barrier solver's two candidate-filter
kernels now forward candidate overflow to its existing failure flag instead of
silently accepting a truncated broad phase. A duplicate-triangle fixture exercises
candidate overflow with no eligible non-adjacent exact contacts.

`make test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu` passes **11 GPU tests**: two new retained
LBVH tests, all seven existing LBVH/collision-pipeline regressions, and two barrier
consumer tests. `make check-all` passes with the existing unused test-helper
warning. Evidence is in
[`benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`](benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/).
The strengthened duplicate-triangle overflow fixture is separately recorded in
`overflow-regression.log`. Tests cover 100 refits in one encoder with changing
device AABBs, pairs compared against expected sets, preserved root, zero LBVH
pair collections and unchanged three bind groups; 130 coincident primitives
emit 8,385 candidates into a fixed 64-slot output without resizing; subsequent
host growth/refit recovers the complete set. Single/empty transitions and topology
mismatch rejection are also covered. Diagnostics count only LBVH bind groups and
host pair collections, not radix-sort resources or the entire GPU runtime.

This is **not GPU rigid contact/friction completion**. The rigid GPU constructor
still rejects colliders. Device shape-AABB production, retained GJK/EPA dispatch
consuming a device count, narrow-phase fallback/fault policy, contact/material
assembly and articulated normal/tangent response remain unimplemented in that
runtime. At this checkpoint, LBVH build/refit WGSL also documented a cross-workgroup
non-atomic visibility dependency; passing RTX 4080 tests is not a portable WebGPU
memory-model proof. The ordered-level repair below supersedes that implementation.
The sparse build timing regressions are not the plan's mixed
contact/friction performance matrix. Full-workspace benchmark certification remains
open as described above.

## P4 retained convex narrow-phase checkpoint

`ResidentNarrowPhase` now binds uploaded shape geometry, one or more device pose
buffers, candidate arrays and the device-emitted pair count. Its `encode` method
adds GJK and EPA passes to a caller-owned encoder without creating resources,
uploading, submitting or reading back. It reuses the existing algorithms through
shared per-pair shader functions; legacy dispatch APIs retain their behavior.
Construction validates buffer availability/capacity and device dispatch/storage
limits. Rebuild the object whenever any bound model, pose or pair buffer changes.

The two passes dispatch over fixed capacity and consume the actual count on GPU.
Retired overlap/contact slots are cleared, so count shrinkage cannot expose old
contacts. The 64-byte EPA result format remains normal/depth, two witnesses and
status. Simplex slots are valid only where the current GJK overlap equals one.
Five buffers, two compute pipelines, and `5 + pose_buffer_count` bind groups are
retained. `resource_counts` describes those owned/retained objects; it is not an
allocator trace or whole-runtime resource certification.

A sticky device status word reports capacity overflow (`1`), invalid shape/body
indices (`2`), unsupported shapes or GJK nonconvergence (`4`), EPA nonconvergence
(`8`), and non-finite inputs/results (`16`). Flags accumulate until an explicitly
encoded reset. Consumers must reject results whenever this word is nonzero;
there is no host geometry fallback in this component. The existing coincident
capsule/box EPA failure is now specifically tested to set bit 8 while retaining
the per-pair fallback status. This exposes the current algorithm limitation rather
than silently treating the pair as separated or substituting a CPU contact.

Five new actual-GPU tests pass:

- 100 queued pose/AABB-copy → retained LBVH refit → GJK → EPA sequences in one
  submission, using two pose bindings and changing overlap/separation/direction.
  Box penetration depth and normal meet the analytic gates; no host pair collection
  or per-substep readback occurs. The AABBs are supplied snapshots, not yet generated
  from shape poses by a production device bounds kernel.
- 130 pairs across three workgroups, alternating endpoint order, followed by count
  shrinkage to one and zero. Depth, normal/witness orientation and retired slots
  are checked.
- Overflow, invalid candidate indices, unsupported plane geometry, NaN poses,
  sticky status and explicit reset, including fault reporting with zero live pairs.
- Missing/undersized buffers, empty pose alternatives and invalid capacities.
- Actual EPA nonconvergence reaches the sticky device fault without CPU fallback.

The expanded `make test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu` lane passes **23 GPU tests**
and `make check-all` passes (existing unused test-helper warning only). The complete
terminal run is `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/narrow-full-final.log`.
An earlier `narrow-full.log` stopped during solver compilation and is not counted
as a completed lane. Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` pass. No dependency
pins, branches or commits changed.

The rigid GPU runtime still rejects colliders. Remaining integration includes
device shape-AABB generation, collision mask/exclusion filtering, plane/other
required geometry and robust degeneracy handling, manifold/material assembly,

## P4 device bounds and ordered LBVH dependency repair

`ResidentShapeBounds` now generates world AABBs from live device body poses and
authored collider transforms. CPU construction compiles only local geometry bounds
and parameters; no world bounds are computed or uploaded during `encode`.
Sphere/capsule/cylinder/rounded-cylinder/ellipsoid bounds use analytic extents,
cones use the existing conservative cylindrical bound, and other finite geometry
uses its transformed local box. Planes retain infinite bounds instead of an
arbitrary world-space cutoff. The output feeds retained LBVH refitting directly.
All inputs/outputs are retained; each call appends one pass without allocations,
uploads, submission, mapping or status reset. The shared sticky status catches
invalid body indices, non-finite transforms and finite-bound overflow. Authored
nonzero dimensions/margins outside normal f32 representability are rejected.

Roundoff padding includes the original parent/local translation magnitudes, not
only the final center. Otherwise large opposing translations can cancel to a small
center while their f32 conversion error remains large enough to miss a collider.
This padding enlarges broad-phase bounds only; it is not physical contact depth.
Ellipsoid extent norms are range-scaled to avoid squaring tiny/large dimensions.

Four new GPU tests pass: 120 mixed analytic/triangle/static/plane shapes over seven
rotated frames and scales `1e-30`, `1e-4`, `1`, `1e30` contain CPU f64 bounds;
large-translation cancellation and explicit margin remain conservative; invalid
poses/indices accumulate faults and clear invalid output; and an infinite plane
still pairs with bodies at `1e9`/`2e9` through actual device bounds and LBVH refitting.
The existing 100-substep geometry chain now uploads only pose snapshots and computes
its AABBs on device before broad-phase/GJK/EPA. Generic mesh/hull/heightfield/SDF
local-box support is implemented but not individually certified by these tests.

The first expanded regression run failed the legacy collision-pipeline test:
**CPU 1,440 contacts, GPU 1,183** (`device-bounds-full.log`). Inspection confirmed
that both old LBVH construction and refitting published non-atomic node data via
cross-workgroup atomic arrival counters, without a guaranteed publication barrier.
The exact failing GPU tree was not captured, so the specific scheduling sequence
behind that observed mismatch is not claimed as proven.

That unsafe dependency is removed, not hidden by retries. The hierarchy now uses
independently constructed complete-binary nodes over the Morton-sorted leaves.
Leaf indices `[0,n)` and the 48-byte public node layout are unchanged; internal
nodes occupy `[n,2n-1)`. Refitting writes all leaves, then processes each internal
heap level deepest-to-root in a separate ordered dispatch. No same-pass invocation
reads another invocation's newly written bounds. Retained dynamic-offset uniforms
encode the level schedule, so the resident path adds no per-step resources or host
synchronization. The old arrival-counter buffer and blanket node-zero upload are
removed. The former `lbvh.wgsl` is replaced by `lbvh_balanced.wgsl`.

The original collision-count regression now repeats 32 builds. A new topology test
covers 20 sizes from 1 through 257 (including workgroup/power-of-two boundaries),
three build/refit frames each, exact brute-force pair sets/counts, every parent-child
link, all node visits and every internal AABB union. Existing sparse timing gates
remain unchanged: the completed lane measured best 3.49 ms for 10,648 shapes and
21.68 ms for 103,823 shapes. These are component wall-clock regressions, not the
plan's 1,000-step mixed-scene GPU-timestamp matrix.

`make test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu` passes **28 GPU tests**, followed by
`make check-all` with only the existing unused test-helper warning. The three
`soft_vt_contact_gpu` tests also pass against the retained public node layout,
including 480/600-step cloth contact and 60-step CPU/GPU parity. Logs are
`device-bounds-ordered-full.log`, `ordered-topology-final.log` and
`ordered-soft-vt-consumer.log` under the same contact checkpoint directory.
Formatting and `git diff --check` pass; no pins, branches or commits changed.

The GPU rigid runtime still rejects colliders. Next integration work is device
collision permission/exclusion filtering, required plane/manifold geometry,
material/contact assembly, articulated normal/tangent response and runtime
fault/rollback/reaction handling. Device bounds and a reliable broad/narrow chain
do not close P4 or the full `MOLLA_PRIMITIVES.md` objective.

## P4 retained device collision-permission checkpoint

`ResidentNarrowPhase` now applies model collision permissions on GPU before shape
support/GJK/EPA evaluation. Its default route excludes sensors from solid contact.
`with_collision_options` additionally accepts sensor-overlap opt-in and extra
shape exclusions. It matches CPU rules for `COLLIDES`, same-body and static/static
pairs, world partitioning (including negative/global world IDs), both directional
membership/mask intersections and sorted canonical shape exclusions. Plane/plane
pairs are dropped as in CPU broad-phase enumeration. Invalid candidate indices
remain faults rather than being silently filtered away.

Construction validates and packs shape flags/groups/masks/worlds, merges model
and extra exclusions, canonicalizes endpoint order and deduplicates pairs. Device
evaluation performs an exclusion binary search without per-contact CPU work or
readback. A compiled scene already expands joint-owned, explicit body and stable
collider exclusions into model shape pairs; the GPU component consumes that table
instead of creating a second ownership policy. Forbidden candidates retain zero
overlap/contact output. Unsupported geometry only faults when an admitted pair
actually reaches narrow phase. Permissions are compiled metadata: recreate this
component after a relevant model/membership/flag/world/exclusion edit.

The narrow-phase object now retains **seven buffers**, two pipelines and
`5 + pose_buffer_count` bind groups (two additional buffers hold permissions and
exclusions). No additional pass, per-step resource creation or per-step permission
upload is required. Candidate capacity still applies before filtering: an
overflowed broad phase remains an explicit fault even if some candidates would
eventually be excluded.

## P4 retained plane-manifold checkpoint

Implemented device analytic plane routing in `ResidentNarrowPhase`, alongside
the retained convex GJK/EPA route. Sphere, box, capsule, cylinder, cone and
ellipsoid plane pairs now produce device contact points without a CPU fallback.
The plane route follows the CPU primitive sampling rules: one sphere/ellipsoid
point, two capsule endpoints, up to four deepest box corners, ten cylinder
samples and five cone samples. It handles either endpoint order and composed
body/collider/plane transforms. Box reduction is stable for equal device depths.

The prepared component retains a ten-slot, 64-byte-per-point manifold buffer and
a count per candidate pair. Each point stores normal/depth, endpoint witnesses
and status in the existing EPA layout. The original `contact_buffer()` exposes
the first point for compatibility. Convex EPA contacts also populate the new
manifold/count buffers. Every inactive point and pair slot is cleared each
dispatch, including after the device candidate count shrinks. The overlap code
`3` identifies the analytic plane route, not a confirmed contact; consumers must
use the manifold count. Simplex contents remain valid only for overlap code `1`.

Preparation checks manifold storage capacity and requires sixteen storage
bindings per shader stage. Resource counts are now nine owned buffers,
`pose_bindings + 5` retained bind groups and two pipelines. `encode()` still only
records two retained passes, with no upload, allocation, submission or readback.
This larger fixed-capacity manifold allocation/clearing cost has not passed the
plan's full performance matrix.

**CPU reference correction:** capsule-plane contact midpoints previously used
the plane normal instead of the capsule-to-plane contact normal, placing the
contact on the wrong side of each endpoint sphere. Corrected that sign and added
analytic point assertions: a horizontal radius-0.3 capsule centered at y=0.2 over
y=0 has midpoint y=-0.05, not y=0.45. Also corrected the misleading declaration
that four points was the maximum for every CPU primitive pair; it is the retained
box manifold limit, while existing cylinder/cone routines emit more points.

## P4 curved plane grazing-contact repair

The new analytic regression reproduced the remaining sampled-rim hole: a
radius-0.3, half-height-0.7 cylinder penetrating a plane with normal
`normalize(1, 1, 1)` by 0.01 returned **zero CPU contacts**. A cone has the same
base-rim gap. The preserved failure is
`benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/curved-grazing-before.log`.

Both CPU and retained GPU plane generation now evaluate the lowest radial point
on each cylinder disk, and on the cone base disk, in addition to the existing
samples. CPU rounded cylinders apply their border offset to these points too.
An extra support point is emitted whenever it penetrates and that disk's samples
do not, regardless of penetration size. When samples already penetrate, the
extra point is emitted if it improves their deepest depth by more than `1e-6`
times the shape dimension scale. That relative threshold merges near-redundant
support samples; it does not suppress a contact that all disk samples missed.

An initial single-support implementation exposed a second ambiguity: for a
cylinder parallel to the plane, tiny CPU/f64 versus GPU/f32 signs of axial
direction picked opposite end disks. The final implementation evaluates both
disks separately, preserves their axial span and passes geometric parity without
weakening the oracle. The intermediate failure is retained in `curved-first.log`.
Ordinary and rounded cylinders can now emit up to twelve points; cones up to six.
`RESIDENT_MANIFOLD_POINTS` and the WGSL stride are **twelve**, superseding the
previous ten-slot checkpoint. Tests derive byte strides from the public constant.
The retained pipeline/resource counts and explicit fault behavior are unchanged.

The CPU cylinder/cone support maps also normalize radial directions by their
largest component rather than treating every direction below an absolute `1e-12`
as axial. Cone support comparisons scale both direction and dimensions. This
preserves support under finite direction rescaling and avoids squared-norm
underflow/overflow in this route; it does not certify all other support maps.

```

## P4 retained GPU normal-force and material-row checkpoint

Added `molla_solvers::normal_contact_gpu::ResidentNormalContacts`, its WGSL kernel
and a GPU regression lane in the existing contact-pipeline Make target. The
`molla-solvers/gpu` feature now enables `molla-geometry/gpu` for the retained
producer/consumer path. Root manifests, dependency pins and environment files
were not changed.

Preparation packs per-shape material/combine-rule/body/flag/surface-velocity
metadata and body COM/flags. It rejects malformed lengths, membership, capacities,
storage limits, nonfinite parameters and nonzero values outside normal f32 range.
The device passes consume candidate/manifold counts and twelve-slot EPA-layout
manifolds directly; no CPU contact extraction is required. The output consists of
128-byte `NormalContactRow` records and 32-byte world-COM body wrenches.

Each row contains midpoint/depth, normalized normal/load, separate combined
static/dynamic coefficients, restitution, shape/body endpoints, relative point
velocity, relative world conveyor velocity, normal force on B and the averaged
penalty parameters. Combine-rule priority matches the CPU, including independent
coefficient channels and legacy scalar fallback. Fixed endpoints have zero
physical velocity; prescribed kinematic motion remains in relative velocity;
surface velocity is rotated by the owning body, not the collider. Sensors,
disabled shapes, same-body contacts and pairs without dynamic endpoints do not
apply forces. This layer expects collision permissions already enforced by the
narrow-phase producer; it does not duplicate joint/exclusion ownership policy.

The normal law matches the current CPU predictor:
`force = stiffness * depth + damping * max(-relative_normal_speed, 0)`.
There is no tangential impulse or authored restitution impulse in this component.
Friction/restitution channels are transported for subsequent stages, not claimed
as a friction solution. Forces use the shared midpoint and opposite endpoint
signs; torques are measured about each body's world COM. Gathered output includes
the supplied external wrench. That base input must remain separate from generated
normal forces so repeated substeps cannot accumulate old contact forces.

Three retained passes reset body incidence heads, generate rows and insert unique
contact-endpoint links, then gather per-body wrenches. Link traversal starts only
after the producer pass completes. No cross-workgroup counter is used to publish
ordinary data within a single pass. Scratch is bounded by body count and candidate
capacity; gathering follows incident contacts rather than scanning all contacts
for every body. Contact slots have deterministic pair/point indexing. Atomic
insertion order can change floating-point summation order; bitwise force/trajectory
determinism is not claimed. The component retains seven buffers,
`state_bindings + 3` bind groups and three pipelines. `encode()` records passes
only, with no buffer/pipeline allocation, upload, submission, mapping or polling.

The narrow-phase shared status remains sticky. New bits are 32 for invalid contact
input, 64 for nonfinite/overflowed response and 128 for invalid/overflowed/
underflowed coefficient combination. Faulted results must be rejected as a whole.
Inactive/retired rows are cleared, incidence heads are reset every dispatch, and
zero-contact output reverts to the supplied external forces. Material/model edits
require reconstruction of the prepared metadata.

  test-primitives-friction-cpu test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu check-all
```

- Synthetic manifold response matches the CPU penalty oracle across all ordered
  pairs of eight shapes, varying point counts across workgroups, all combine

- Capacity/index/count, malformed normal, nonfinite external wrench, normal-force
  overflow, coefficient product overflow/underflow and explicit reset are tested.
  Zero-contact dispatches retain previous faults and cannot retain old forces.
- One encoder queues 100 device bounds -> LBVH -> manifold -> normal-force

- A separate **1,000-step, 1 ms GPU Featherstone drop-and-settle test** consumes

## P4 retained coupled GPU Coulomb-disk checkpoint

Added `molla_solvers::coulomb_disk_gpu::ResidentCoulombDisks`, a retained solver
for device-provided contact islands. It minimizes
`0.5 * lambda^T * G * lambda + free^T * lambda` over one circular impulse disk
per contact. Coupled off-diagonal Gram terms are retained; this is not an
independent point or axis clamp. Fixed per-island slots hold the square Gram,
free tangential velocities and sixteen-byte static/dynamic impulse-radius plus
pre-predictor-slip records. The radii are `mu * normal_force * dt`, not raw
coefficients. Caller-owned island/contact counts stay on device.

Preparation creates four buffers, one bind group and one pipeline. `encode()`
only records dispatch, without allocation, upload, submission, mapping or polling.
One invocation handles each island using scaled accelerated projected iterations
and adaptive restart. A scaled modified-Cholesky screen checks finite/symmetric/
positive-semidefinite input within numerical tolerances; it is not a strict
symbolic PSD certificate. Zero-response matrices use the linear disk minimizer.
Static trials that leave slip above the CPU capture band switch to dynamic radii
and resolve. An initially moving point can stop on its dynamic disk and use the
static disk in the next substep. No warm-start/tangential spring state is cached.

Solutions contain impulse, residual slip, selected radius, regime, iteration count
and physical velocity KKT residual. Shared sticky bits are `1<<16` for input,
`1<<17` for nonfinite/unrepresentable arithmetic, `1<<18` for the matrix screen
and `1<<19` for nonconvergence/energy rejection. Per-island diagnostics retain
fault, iterations, residual bits and failure phase while the shared status is
nonzero. Output slots clear even on sticky faults; consumers must reject the
whole result whenever shared status is nonzero. Explicit status reset permits
new solutions and resets diagnostics. Host preparation validates storage usage,
buffer sizes, capacities, arithmetic overflow and binding/dispatch limits.

Numerical development exposed two separate issues, without relaxing acceptance:

- Single-precision division/normalization in radial complementarity falsely
  rejected the zero-Gram disk minimizer at `5.4249796e-7`. Compensated radius
  quotient/norm arithmetic and scaled angular residuals evaluate the rounded
  published impulse rather than only the normalized iterate.
- A rotated `1e-30` reciprocal-scale case reported device residual
  `8.028659e-8` but an independent f64 check of the actual output found
  `1.0885896964075985e-7`. A tighter target alone was insufficient: strict
  half-tolerance acceptance stalled, while a 75% target still accepted another
  point with host residual `1.1218600603374719e-7`. In that case the GPU's
  supposedly compensated slip exactly matched the naive f32 sum. The final
  implementation retains physical impulses and rounds compensation intermediates
  through atomic scratch bit storage. This prevents those intermediate rounding
  boundaries being erased; actual compiler instruction-level behavior was not
  captured. Device iteration/acceptance uses 75% of the configured tolerance.
  The external test limit remains `1e-7 m/s`; an all-input f32 error proof and
  performance certification of the atomic scratch implementation remain open.

The focused GPU lane has four tests:

1. 130 islands across three workgroups compare seven fixture classes against the
   actual CPU disk solver: anisotropic SPD, singular repeated contacts, zero Gram,
   static-to-dynamic switching, four-pad rigid COM wrench response and a coupled
   six-contact SPD system. Device counts shrink `130 -> 1 -> 0` in one encoder;
   retired slots clear. Singular solutions compare response/objective, not a
   nonunique raw impulse. Peak sampled iterations were 24.
2. Thirty independent tangent-basis rotation/contact-permutation/reciprocal-scale
   variants span `G/scale`, `cap*scale`, with scale `1e-30` through `1e30`.
   Normalized impulses match the CPU reference and independently reconstructed
   f64 KKT residuals stay below `1e-7`; sampled peak was
   `7.441474108024202e-8 m/s`. Normalized relative-slip energy stays nonpositive
   and agrees with the CPU objective across the same transformations.
3. One hundred queued input updates exercise static holding, switching, dynamic
   stopping, re-stick eligibility, reversal, zero coefficients and per-island
   contact-count retirement. These are supplied-input solver fixtures, not body
   integration or sustained GPU loaded-incline acceptance.
4. Malformed constructors, device count overflow, invalid caps, nonfinite data,
   nonsymmetric/indefinite matrices, weighted-matrix overflow/underflow and forced
   one-iteration nonconvergence fail closed. Subsequent empty-count dispatches
   preserve fault diagnostics and clear outputs; explicit reset restores solving.

Evidence lives under `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`:
`disk-invariance.log`, `disk-slip-diagnostic.log`, `disk-kkt-guard.log` and
`disk-sum-diagnostic.log` preserve precision failures. `disk-kkt-margin.log` was
an intermediate pass with a tighter iteration target but the old acceptance
threshold; `disk-full.log` then exposed strict half-tolerance nonconvergence.
`disk-rounded-pass.log` records the final atomic-scratch focused four-test pass.
The final complete contact-pipeline/CPU-friction/check-all rerun is recorded in
`disk-certified.log`.

Final validation on the RTX 4080, with `NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07`:

```text
nix develop --impure -c make \
  fmt-files FMT_ARGS='--config skip_children=true' \
  FILES='crates/molla-solvers/src/coulomb_disk_gpu.rs crates/molla-solvers/src/coulomb_disk_gpu_tests.rs' \
  test-primitives-friction-cpu test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu check-all
```

**36 CPU tests and 43 actual GPU tests passed**, including the four coupled-disk
tests and the existing 1,000-step normal-only drop. `check-all` and tracked
`git diff --check` passed. The pre-existing unused `body_poses` test-helper warning
remains. This was the named regression lane, not the previously stalled full
workspace test/benchmark suite. No commit was made.

**Still partial:** GPU contact island construction, articulated tangent Jacobian
and effective-mass assembly, impulse application/redrift, runtime force/readout,
sleep/reaction/break transactions and joint/contact coupling are not wired to this
core. The runtime collider guard remains unchanged. The normal-only drop test and
these algebraic solver gates do not establish GPU static holding or kinetic
sliding trajectories. P4 and the overall primitives goal remain incomplete.

## P4 deterministic device contact-island checkpoint

Added `contact_islands_gpu::ResidentContactIslands` as the grouping/input boundary
between normal-contact rows and the retained coupled disk solver. Preparation
accepts body-to-articulation ownership and static articulation dependency edges.
World, fixed and prescribed endpoints use an explicit no-response sentinel; they
do not merge unrelated dynamic groups. Dynamic bodies in the same articulated
response group share one owner. These metadata are topology inputs, not per-step
CPU contact extraction, and must be rebuilt after ownership/dependency changes.

Five component passes clear all counts/mappings, join articulated response groups,
label eligible contact roots, compact root metadata, and scatter fixed island
slots. A retained stable radix sort runs between compaction and scattering.
Atomic unions only lower parent indices, selecting the minimum articulation as
the canonical root. Root order is deterministic; stable sorting gives ascending
original normal-row order within each island. No atomic append ordering becomes
the solver's contact indexing. Root compaction is currently a serial device
prefix over articulations and scatter uses sorted-key lower bounds; large-scene
timing/performance certification remains open.

Positive-load active normal rows join response groups even when their friction
coefficient is zero. Only positive-load rows with nonzero static coefficient and
at least one responding endpoint occupy tangent slots. Explicit dependencies
can join components with no direct frictional edge. Fixed/kinematic/world
boundaries may be shared by independent components without joining them.

Outputs are device island count, per-island contact counts, fixed-slot original
row indices, original-row `(island, local_contact)` mapping, articulation-to-island
mapping and canonical roots. Inactive/retired mappings use `u32::MAX`. Counts clear
on every dispatch even with a prior sticky fault. Input faults use `1<<20` and
capacity faults `1<<21`; actual excessive counts remain visible while scatter
refuses to publish a truncated solve. Consumers must reject nonzero shared status.
Preparation validates ownership/dependency indices, positive capacities, buffer
usage/sizes and dispatch/storage limits. Resources are twenty retained buffers,
seven bind groups and eight pipelines including the stable sort. Encoding records
seventeen ordered passes with no upload, allocation, submission, mapping or polling.

`RadixSortKernel::prepare` now returns an independent `RadixSortDispatch` using
the existing count/scan/scatter shaders. Each prepared sort owns fixed-length
scratch and immutable per-digit uniforms through its bindings; old dispatches,
kernel growth, another prepared length or dropping the kernel cannot overwrite
its configuration. The existing one-shot dispatch API is unchanged. This adds no
dependency/pin or environment-file change.

Validation evidence under `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`:

- `islands-stress.log`: eight real-GPU radix tests (seven existing plus one retained
  multi-length test) and three new real-GPU contact-island tests pass.
- Prepared lengths 1, 257 and 513 run sixty queued stable sorts after growing and
  dropping their source kernel. Duplicate/all-equal/high-byte keys match the CPU
  stable reference; independent scratch/uniform lifetime is exercised.
- One hundred queued contact graphs over 160 articulations, two bodies per
  articulation and 512 normal-row slots match the CPU union/packing oracle exactly.
  Cases include dependency edges, fixed/kinematic/world boundaries, endpoint
  reversal, zero coefficients/load, inactive rows, splitting, shrinking and empty
  graphs. Every retired slot is checked, not only final counts.
- Twelve queued ascending, reversed and permuted 1,025-articulation chains span
  workgroups and pack up to 2,048 contacts. Alternating zero-friction chain edges
  still connect the response groups; all output ordering matches the CPU oracle.
- Too many islands/contacts retain excessive counts and fault rather than clamp.
  Invalid endpoints, nonfinite coefficients/loads and malformed active flags fault;
  a later empty dispatch preserves status and retires outputs, and explicit reset
  restores the valid mapping. Invalid host capacities/ownership/dependencies and
  undersized row buffers are rejected before dispatch.
- `islands-producer-chain.log`: the existing 100-sequence GPU bounds -> LBVH ->
  manifold -> normal-force test now continues through island construction. The
  box's four loaded manifold corners map to `[0,1,2,3]` in one island; separation
  clears counts and mappings. This has no intermediate readback and no added
  tangential integration. The normal-only 1,000-step drop remains a separate gate.

The complete CPU-friction/contact-pipeline/check-all rerun is recorded in
`islands-full.log`: **36 CPU tests and 54 actual GPU tests passed**, and `check-all`
passed with the existing unused `body_poses` helper warning. The command was
`NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c make test-primitives-friction-cpu
test-primitives-contact-pipeline-gpu check-all`. A subsequent empty-articulation
edge check and its focused rerun are recorded in `islands-empty-articulation.log`;
all eleven focused GPU tests and `check-all` passed. The unused dummy articulation
mapping now clears to the same no-island sentinel.
Tracked `git diff --check` passes. No commits or dependency/environment changes
were made; this is not a full-workspace test/benchmark certification.

**Next required boundary:** compile actual scene articulation ownership and
dependency metadata with the articulated mass/Jacobian preparation, assemble
point tangents and `J M^-1 J^T` from device geometry and predicted state, consume
these deterministic row slots in the disk core, apply generalized impulses and
redrift, then wire the full production transaction. Contact island construction
is not constraint solving: dependency grouping does not enforce external distance,
cone or stop rows. The runtime collider guard remains unchanged; P4/P5/P6 and the
overall primitives goal remain incomplete.

## P4 articulated GPU response and loaded-trajectory checkpoint

Added `contact_response_gpu::ResidentContactResponse`. Preparation derives actual
body/articulation ownership from model topology, excludes immovable endpoints,
packs COM metadata and prepares the existing GPU CRBA and COM-Jacobian kernels
for every retained input-pose binding. Unowned dynamic bodies, malformed topology,
unsupported kernel topology, invalid storage/capacities and nonrepresentable
authored mass/inertia/COM metadata fail explicitly. Caller-supplied dependency
edges are passed to device contact grouping. Rebuild after metadata, dependencies
or bound buffers change; dependency grouping is not enforcement of loop constraints.

`ResidentContactIslands` now additionally publishes deterministic articulation
member offsets/indices. Its serial compaction builds this CSR in ascending member
order, so response assembly walks only member articulations rather than scanning
all articulations for every island. The original GPU/CPU exact-mapping tests now
check the CSR and retired entries too. Island preparation now retains **22 buffers**
instead of 20; the bind-group and pipeline counts remain seven and eight.

The response component records island production, retained mass/Jacobian passes,
tangent geometry, per-articulation mass factor/projection, per-island Gram/free-slip
assembly, coupled disks, generalized impulse application and world-impulse readout.
COM wrench projection sums both signed endpoints, including when both belong to
the same articulation. Whitened rows form a symmetric `J M^-1 J^T`; the same factors
map disk impulses back to generalized-rate deltas. Initial slip comes from normal
rows including conveyor-relative velocity, with `J * (predicted_rates-input_rates)`
added only for responding DOFs. Corrected rates preserve untouched articulations.
The component uses old/input geometry, matching the CPU predictor/redrift policy.

Caller-owned device timestep and shared sticky status remain resident. New faults
are `1<<22` for response input, `1<<23` for unsupported/invalid mass factors, and
`1<<24` for nonfinite/unrepresentable response. Outputs are cleared before each
recorded chain, including sticky-fault calls; every consumer must reject nonzero
status. Corrected rates are not automatically published to a runtime state.
World tangent impulse on B is stored in original normal-row order; A receives
its negative. Existing normal force and restitution authoring were not replaced.

Mass capability remains explicit: coordinate-null rows get zero response, while
nonzero Cholesky pivots at or below `1e-6` of the matrix scale fail. Oblique rank
deficiency therefore fails rather than becoming a spurious very large inverse.
The current cutoff also rejects some ill-conditioned/scale-stressed full-rank
systems. General spectral/null-space GPU response and its broader scale gates
remain required; this is not claimed as complete mass/inertia certification.

The new GPU lane, `make test-primitives-contact-response-gpu`, covers:

1. Twelve queued configurations of an offset-COM free-root/hinge articulation
   contacting a separate free articulation, with fixed and prescribed boundaries,
   conveyors, arbitrary normals and endpoint reversal. Against the actual CPU
   articulated/friction routines, peak Gram error is `5.680281103259688e-7` and
   corrected-rate error about `3.89e-7`. No independent-body approximation is used.
2. Seven bad-input sequences exercise invalid/nonfinite/subnormal timestep,
   malformed normal, nonfinite point/predicted rate and cap overflow. Sticky status
   survives an empty-contact dispatch, outputs retire, explicit reset restores the
   valid result, and malformed constructor capacities/buffers fail before encoding.
3. Coordinate-aligned null inertia produces the analytic zero-response axis;
   rotating that rank deficiency into an oblique basis produces the explicit mass
   fault with no corrected rates published.
4. A **10,000-step, 1 ms GPU loaded-box hold**, with no sleeping or intermediate
   readback, runs bounds -> LBVH -> manifolds -> normal COM wrenches -> Featherstone
   predictor -> articulated friction -> corrected-rate redrift. A 2 kg box on a
   horizontal plane receives gravity resolved at 0.3 rad; this is the rotated-frame
   incline equivalent. Four corners use `1e5 N/m` stiffness and `300 N s/m` damping,
   coefficients 0.6/0.2 and initial normal equilibrium. Sampled peak tangential
   displacement is `2.2777468984713778e-5 m`, post-first-second creep
   `5.64266884328959e-7 m`, CPU position error `5.668846621358381e-7 m`, and velocity
   error `1.3944007833321154e-5 m/s`. Gates remain `2e-4 m` peak displacement,
   `1e-6 m` creep, `3e-5 m` CPU position error and `2e-3 m/s` velocity error.
5. A **1,000-step kinetic slide** at 0.5 rad, coefficients 0.4/0.2 and initial
   tangent speed 0.1 m/s measures acceleration over 0.2–1.0 s. Sampled acceleration
   is `2.981366813182831 m/s^2` versus `2.98134754727832 m/s^2` analytically, against
   the unchanged 2% gate. CPU position/velocity errors are approximately
   `1.81e-6 m` and `2.28e-5 m/s`. This is a moving slide, not yet a GPU zero-speed
   breakaway/stop/re-stick/reversal trajectory matrix.

The first holding trial used softer `1e4 N/m`, `100 N s/m` support and reached
`2.2537134645972404e-4 m` initial displacement, failing the `2e-4 m` bound while
matching the CPU within `8.81e-8 m`. The normal stiffness/damping were changed to
the established CPU holding-fixture values, not the acceptance bound. Both the
initial elastic displacement and later creep are measured separately.

The integrated slide exposed further disk precision issues, preserved in logs:
the previous 75% internal target stalled at step 120 (`8.2387835e-8` residual);
physical-radius reconstruction advanced to step 248, and compensated high/low
residual evaluation advanced to step 342 (`1.00368815e-7`). Active disk boundaries
now reconstruct impulses at the actual physical radius, avoiding cap/scale round
trips. KKT evaluation retains compensated slip low parts, atomic-rounded radial
quotients/norm terms and compensated angular products. Near-converged stalls get
bounded anti-slip direction and adjacent-float refinement, minimizing maximum
residual then residual merit. The external KKT gate remains **`1e-7 m/s`**; the
old blanket 75% margin is replaced by a one-part-per-million rounding guard.
Existing 30 basis/permutation/reciprocal-scale cases still receive independent f64
checks of published impulses (sampled peak `9.977477124566751e-8`). No tolerance
increase or unchecked iteration-budget success path was introduced.

Evidence: `response-loaded.log` preserves the softer-support failure;
`response-hold-slide-faults.log`, `response-boundary-radius.log` and
`response-compensated-residual.log` preserve kinetic convergence failures.
`response-polish.log` records the focused nine-test pass. The final complete
CPU-friction/contact-pipeline/check-all rerun, including independent per-step f64
KKT/energy checks of the integrated published impulses, is in `response-full.log`
under `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`.

The complete named lanes passed **36 CPU tests and 59 actual GPU tests**, followed
by `check-all`. A subsequent five-test response rerun and `check-all` also passed
after adding orientation parity (`response-orientation.log`). Peak quaternion
angle error was `1.2990531157078367e-7 rad` for holding and
`2.9802322387695313e-8 rad` for sliding, against the `1e-3 rad` gate. Independent
host-f64 reconstruction checked every integrated step's published impulses:
peak KKT residuals were `9.989676738694049e-8 m/s` and
`9.429168919133732e-8 m/s`, respectively, below the unchanged `1e-7 m/s` gate.
The same checks enforce circular caps and nonpositive relative-slip energy.
`git diff --check` passed. This is not a claim that the full workspace test or
previously stalled synchronized benchmark passes.

**Still partial:** these integration tests explicitly copy corrected rates and
invoke redrift with separate queue submissions. Geometry/contact and Featherstone
status are checked separately, not wired as one production halt/rollback boundary.
`rigid_world_gpu.rs::validate` still rejects colliders. Production transaction,
sleep/wake/mutation/readout/reaction/break wiring, unified joint/contact constraints,
restitution, general null-space response, wider scales/steps/materials and full
resource/performance certification remain open. The new device trajectories are
real progress toward P4, not completion of P4/P5/P6 or the overall goal.

## P4 GPU transition and radial-residual follow-up

Loaded breakaway and stop/re-stick/reversal trajectories exposed an acceptance
error in the device disk residual. A published axial impulse one f32 step inside
its cap had reconstructed KKT error `1.0000458558827909e-7 m/s`, while the device
reported `8.037167e-8 m/s`; the reversal case reproduced the same discrepancy.
The direct GPU boundary-gap probe reproduced the underlying quotient-based
squared-radius error (`1.1920928955078125e-7` versus host-f64
`1.3490472606667887e-7`). These failures are preserved in `response-transitions.log`,
`response-transition-diagnostics.log` and `disk-gap-before.log` under
`benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`.

The radial residual now computes the compensated squared-radius difference before
division, using power-of-two scaling, explicitly rounded subtraction intermediates
and product remainders. The 585-case GPU probe covers adjacent-float inside/on/outside
radii, 65 angles and three scales; peak absolute squared-gap error is
`1.9210221126225147e-14` (`disk-gap-squared.log`). The external velocity KKT gate is
unchanged. The final named-lane rerun is recorded in `transition-full.log`:
**36 CPU tests and 61 GPU tests passed; one new GPU breakaway test failed**.
All previously passing tests, the new radial-gap probe and the new stop/re-stick
test pass. `make check-all` passes separately (`transition-check.log`), with the
existing unused `body_poses` helper warning. `git diff --check` also passes.

The new breakaway fixture ramps COM force from 0 to 8 N over 0.5 s, holds to 1 s,
ramps to 13 N by 2 s and holds to 2.5 s. Its 2 kg box has 0.6/0.2 coefficients
and 19.62 N nominal support, so the static threshold is 11.772 N. Ramping the
initial load avoids confusing an abrupt compliant-support transient with the
quasi-static threshold. Settled holding is checked over 0.7–1 s. GPU sliding starts
at step 1762 (11.81 N), versus CPU step 1763. Both use the same authored force
schedule. The independently reconstructed GPU KKT residual remains below `1e-7`,
but peak CPU/GPU position error reaches `2.9166793914340064e-3 m` and velocity
error `4.708086026111094e-3 m/s`. The new regression therefore **fails**; it retains
the trajectory checks rather than accepting event timing alone. This also exceeds
the plan's 1 mm controlled-trajectory scale. The threshold-parity cause is not yet
isolated; `breakaway-regimes.log` records the transition frames. Do not claim GPU
breakaway certification or a green complete contact-pipeline lane from this work.

The stop/re-stick fixture starts at 0.3 m/s under +1 N COM force, changes to -1 N
at 1 s, then -12.5 N at 2 s. It measures displacement throughout the sub-threshold
force reversal, with a bounded 0.25 s compliant settling window before requiring
small COM speed again. Each step checks the published disk caps, reconstructed
KKT residual and relative-slip energy; sampled regime sets compare against CPU.
Force schedules are uploaded once and copied device-to-device before normal-force
assembly, with no intermediate contact/state readback.

Stop/re-stick/reversal passes: maximum displacement across the sub-threshold
reversal is `7.621943950653076e-6 m`, peak CPU position error
`2.0124735876108605e-6 m`, orientation error `5.960464477539063e-8 rad` and velocity
error `1.8094133011957338e-5 m/s`. Independent per-step KKT reconstruction peaks at
`9.826727717226071e-8 m/s`. The final super-threshold reversal slides in the opposite
direction and satisfies the 2% analytic acceleration gate. These remain test-wired
device trajectories, not production runtime transaction/collider certification.

## P4 compensated-coordinate investigation

Replay of the recorded GPU Gram/free-slip/cap inputs through the CPU disk solver
agrees with the GPU transition decision (`breakaway-inputs.log`). The two backends
reach different input states before transition. GPU height originally stayed at
one f32 value while CPU accumulated sub-ULP normal motion. Tightening post-trial
capture from `1e-4` to `1e-7 m/s` was tested and rejected: the established five-second
CPU loaded hold slid about 13 m (`transition-feasibility.log`). The original capture
policy is restored; the tighter rule cannot replace coupled compliant support.

Added explicitly prepared GPU scalar/translation rounding-residue buffers to
Featherstone. Each prepared joint-coordinate buffer owns a separate device residue
buffer. Both predictor and redrift copy residues from the input state before
integration, so redrift replaces rather than accumulates the provisional drift.
Scalar clamps and translational distance/D6 projections clear affected residues.
Quaternion integration is unchanged. Preparation validates unique uploaded state
buffers; later unprepared states fail before dispatch. Callers must reset residues
after coordinate edits or external writers and rebuild after topology changes.
This is an opt-in resident capability, not implicit hidden state keyed only by
floating-point values, and is not yet wired into production runtime transactions.
The first compensated-drift breakaway run still fails trajectory parity at about
2.91 mm, so compensated integration alone is not claimed as the breakaway fix.

`compensated_drift_accumulates_sub_ulp_motion_without_double_redrift` passes across
coordinate scales `1e-6`, `0.5` and `1024`, accumulating 1,000 sub-ULP increments
per run. It checks both single and duplicate redrift, explicit coordinate-edit
reset, duplicate preparation rejection and unprepared-state rejection. The existing
eight-joint-kind drift parity test also passes. Both now run in the complete contact
pipeline lane. Residue buffers are exposed for paired coordinate/residue checkpoint
and restore; reset is a recorded device clear, not a host readback.

The final `compensated-full.log` rerun passes **36 CPU tests and 63 GPU tests**;
the one breakaway trajectory test remains failing. `check-all` passes separately
(`compensated-check-final.log`). With prepared compensation enabled, the loaded hold
has peak displacement `2.276237864862196e-5 m`, post-settling creep
`5.62652530813478e-7 m` and CPU position error `5.660238563278354e-7 m`. The kinetic
slide measures `2.9814093559980392 m/s^2` versus `2.98134754727832 m/s^2`, with CPU
position error `9.486561533091234e-6 m`. Stop/re-stick has sub-threshold reversal
displacement `7.798895239830017e-6 m` and CPU position error
`3.383316103498908e-6 m`. All retain their previous displacement, trajectory,
orientation, velocity, analytic-acceleration and independently reconstructed KKT
gates. These are component/test-wired results; production runtime ownership,
mutation/rollback/sleep integration and the broader precision matrix remain open.

Additional regression validation passes **three GPU scalar/coupled-stop momentum
tests and ten GPU runtime-contract tests**, including atomic fault recovery,
mutation/rebuild, frame/COM/motor parity and warmed resource retention. See
`compensated-runtime-regressions.log`; the warm resource snapshot is
`[76 buffers, 526608 bytes, 12 groups, 3 pipelines, 3 shaders]`. These thirteen tests
exercise the default runtime path, not opt-in compensation ownership. Across the
named lanes and these additional checks, this checkpoint has 36 CPU and 76 GPU
passes, with the one breakaway failure still present. `git diff --check` passes.

A trial computing box-plane depth before world-witness rounding did not resolve
breakaway (alone or with compensated drift), and was reverted. The captured
`breakaway-local-depth.log` and `breakaway-compensated-local-depth.log` are diagnostic
failures, not accepted geometry changes. Future work must compare predictor/contact
input accuracy and near-threshold solver convergence without removing the failing
trajectory check or replacing the compliant holding contract.

## P4 breakaway convergence and compensated-reversal follow-up

Tightening the CPU friction solve to `1e-9` (without changing the `1e-4` capture
band) leaves CPU breakaway at step 1763 and the GPU at step 1762. Peak trajectory
error changes only from about 2.91203 mm to 2.91187 mm. This diagnostic did not
explain the failure; the CPU solver settings were restored. Evidence is in
`breakaway-cpu-1e-9.log` under `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`.

The trajectory harness now preserves the full physical force schedule and duration
under timestep refinement, rather than shortening or weakening the fixture. Before
the coordinate-reversal fix below, runs at 1, 2, 4 and 8 substeps per millisecond
gave CPU/GPU peak position errors of approximately 2.912, 4.351, 2.165 and 1.092 mm
(`breakaway-refinement.log`). Those are historical diagnostic results, superseded
by the final rerun below. Smaller timesteps alone are not accepted as a fix.

A separate drift regression reproduced loss of the compensation residue across
large positive/negative translations: a `1e-6` coordinate returned as zero after
a `+1e12/-1e12` reversal (`coordinate-reversal-before.log`). Coordinate accumulation
now keeps both sum errors and renormalizes the high/low result before publishing
the coordinate. The new reversal test recovers all three authored coordinates
(`1e-6`, `0.5`, `1024`) exactly in f32 across three round trips. All three drift GPU
tests pass, including the existing sub-ULP, repeated-redrift, reset and eight-joint
parity cases (`coordinate-two-sum.log`). This arithmetic fix is distinct from the
still-open breakaway trajectory failure.

An exploratory GPU solve-accuracy run kept the capture band and physical fixture
fixed while lowering only the disk tolerance. At `1e-8`, breakaway still occurs
at step 1762, and step 2255 subsequently reports explicit nonconvergence after
8192 iterations. `breakaway-gpu-accuracy.log` preserves that failure. Tighter GPU
iteration acceptance therefore is not accepted as a trajectory fix; the default
`1e-7` disk gate is unchanged. This exploratory tighter-than-contract run is not
part of the named acceptance lane. The original and timestep-refinement trajectory
regressions remain in that lane, with their displacement gates intact.

The final named-lane rerun (`refinement-full.log`) passes **36 CPU tests and
64 actual GPU tests**, with **two GPU failures**: the original breakaway trajectory
and its timestep-refinement regression. All three drift tests pass. With the
coordinate-reversal fix, the final breakaway measurements are:

| 4 | 2.164896 mm | 0.003478453 m/s | 7052 / 7049 |

The unchanged position/velocity gates are `3e-5 m` and `2e-3 m/s`; all four runs
fail both. The finest run's independently reconstructed per-step KKT peak is
`9.999201393052515e-8`, within the unchanged `1e-7` disk gate. Refinement is not
monotonic and does not establish trajectory parity. Holding, kinetic sliding and
stop/re-stick/reversal still pass, with peak CPU position errors approximately

## P4 compensated FK translations and plane-depth follow-up

Coordinate residues now propagate through Featherstone FK into a separate
per-state `vec4<f32>` body-translation residue buffer. The opt-in preparation binds
both coordinate and pose buffer identities; predictor and redrift copy both residue
buffers from the input state. Fixed/kinematic and inactive states preserve their
input residues. The explicit reset clears both buffers, and callers must checkpoint
both with their high state components. The disabled/default Featherstone arithmetic
path remains unchanged. Quaternion integration and model-parameter precision are
not extended to two-part arithmetic.

`gpu_position_compensation_buffer` exposes these retained body residues.
`ResidentCollisionOptions::plane_position_residues` optionally binds one such buffer
per pose alternative. Analytic plane depths now accumulate relative centers and
support offsets before reducing to f32, rather than subtracting already-rounded
world witnesses. This covers the supported sphere, capsule, box, ellipsoid, cylinder
and cone plane paths. Convex GJK/EPA, published world witnesses and general rotated
arithmetic still use f32; this is not general double-precision collision support.
The plane pass uses each pair's atomic count slot as private rounding scratch and
publishes its final count only after completing the manifold. Invalid residue
counts/sizes fail setup; nonfinite residues produce the existing sticky fault.

The new fixed-frame FK regression reconstructs sub-ULP root and child translations
at three scales, including repeated redrift and residue reset. A new plane regression
uses both endpoint orders, three power-of-two scales and a translated origin at
1024 times the shape scale. The penetration comes entirely from body residues and
is only `1e-9` times that scale. Its first implementation incorrectly returned no
contacts. Diagnostics showed correct incoming low terms but a zero low term after
relative-center addition. Explicitly rounding the TwoSum error before combining it
with subsequent low terms restores all four contacts in every case. The same error
rounding boundary now applies to coordinate and FK sums. Logs:
`position-depth-diagnostic.log`, `position-depth-rounded.log`, and
`position-residue-drift.log`, under the existing contact GPU evidence directory.

This precision extension is **not a breakaway fix**. After the rounding correction,
the focused original trajectory still starts GPU sliding at step 1762 versus CPU
1763, with peak position error `2.9183483213813728e-3 m` and velocity error
`4.7118526933781985e-3 m/s` (`position-breakaway-rounded.log`). The unchanged gates
remain failing. The earlier uncorrected implementation was worse, starting at 1761;
those exploratory results in `position-breakaway.log` and `position-inputs.log`
are superseded.

The final `position-full.log` run passes **36 CPU tests and 66 actual GPU tests**;
the original and refined breakaway trajectory tests remain the **two failures**.
All 13 retained narrow-phase tests and all four drift tests pass, including the new
residue setup/nonfinite checks. `make check-all` exits zero (`position-check.log`).
The current refinement results supersede the previous checkpoint's table:

| Substeps per millisecond | Peak CPU/GPU position error | Peak velocity error | CPU / GPU sliding onset step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2.918348 mm | 0.004711853 m/s | 1763 / 1762 |
| 2 | 2.902705 mm | 0.004627621 m/s | 3526 / 3524 |
| 4 | 1.448567 mm | 0.002329718 m/s | 7052 / 7050 |
| 8 | 2.200544 mm | 0.003471341 m/s | 14105 / 14099 |

The unchanged per-step KKT, energy and cap checks pass, while all four runs still
fail the position/velocity parity gates. Holding, kinetic sliding and reversal pass
with CPU position errors about `5.64e-7 m`, `2.70e-6 m` and `3.24e-6 m`, respectively.
Holding creep after one second is `5.61401068877383e-7 m`. Production collider
dispatch, general rotated/convex precision and the performance matrix remain open.

The additional uncompensated/default-path checks pass **three momentum/stop tests
and ten runtime contract tests**, including mutation, rollback, authored frames,
COM/inertia and warm resource retention (`position-runtime-regressions.log`). The
warm snapshot is `[77 buffers, 526624 bytes, 12 groups, 3 pipelines, 3 shaders]` and
does not grow across the measured warm steps. This checkpoint therefore records
36 CPU and 79 GPU passes across the named lanes and these separate regressions,
plus the two explicit breakaway failures. These are correctness/resource results,
not a performance certification or a full-workspace test pass.

## P4 near-capacity static convergence follow-up

A replay of the live GPU Gram/free/cap inputs found a false-convergence window
before breakaway. At step 1700 the GPU published about `4.53e-7 m/s` slip while the
CPU disk oracle on identical inputs found about `1e-9 m/s`. At step 1754 the GPU
published about `1.60e-5 m/s` versus the oracle's `5.96e-6 m/s`. Reconstructing slip
from the actually applied generalized rates differed from the reported matrix
slip by at most about `2.35e-9 m/s` in the selected pre-transition samples, so that
application rounding did not explain the larger solve discrepancy. The diagnostic
is retained in `replay-breakaway.log`; temporary snapshot/readout instrumentation
was removed after the comparison.

The old radial residual was speed times relative distance from the disk boundary.
It could become small while both the boundary distance and the remaining slip were
still too large for static holding. A new two-contact rank-deficient fixture has a
known zero-slip feasible solution, unequal caps and loads from 80% to 99.99% of
capacity. Across three directions and three reciprocal scales, the old criterion
accepted peak slip `4.288911797138404e-6 m/s`, exceeding the unchanged `1e-7 m/s`
gate (`static-feasibility-before.log`).

The GPU convergence check now also bounds
`min(speed, local_curvature * abs(cap - impulse_length))`, where local curvature is
the infinity-norm bound of the contact's 2x2 diagonal Gram block. The existing
angular, speed-weighted radial, cap, energy and capture checks remain active; no
tolerance, force schedule, coefficient, duration or capture band was relaxed. The
same additional residual is independently reconstructed in f64 by the disk and live
trajectory tests. The 36-case static fixture now has peak slip
`6.717164069414139e-8 m/s`, and the existing disk tests pass
(`static-feasibility-disks.log`).

The CPU barrier fallback also validates the additional radial residual. Its initial
nine-stage solve was rejected by the unchanged loaded-incline test at
`1.5731599931980976e-7`; the barrier continuation now uses eleven stages before
validation. A matching 36-case CPU regression covers the same feasible static
loads. This changes solve accuracy, not capture or contact material semantics.

Before the CPU continuation extension, the focused original breakaway trajectory
passed: both backends first slide at step 1763, peak position error is
`7.02920274513834e-6 m`, and peak velocity error is `2.8716726171143132e-5 m/s`
(`static-feasibility-breakaway.log`). The final CPU/GPU and timestep-refinement
reruns remain the acceptance evidence for the complete current change.

The final current rerun (`static-feasibility-full.log`) passes **37 CPU tests and
14 actual GPU tests**: all six coupled-disk tests and all eight response tests.
Both previous breakaway failures are now passing. The original and refined runs
retain their per-substep f64 KKT/cap/energy checks and physical holding/sliding
checks, with the added radial residual at the same `1e-7` gate:

| Substeps per millisecond | Peak CPU/GPU position error | Peak velocity error | CPU / GPU sliding onset step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 7.038236 micrometres | 0.000028729 m/s | 1763 / 1763 |
| 2 | 8.021342 micrometres | 0.000098510 m/s | 3526 / 3526 |
| 4 | 13.338195 micrometres | 0.000081991 m/s | 7052 / 7052 |
| 8 | 20.315086 micrometres | 0.000100223 m/s | 14105 / 14105 |

All four measured position/velocity errors meet the unchanged `3e-5 m` and
`2e-3 m/s` gates. The holding, slide and reversal cases also pass; holding creep is
`5.615338530000398e-7 m`, and reversal CPU position error is approximately
`3.13e-6 m`. `make check-all` exits zero (`static-feasibility-check.log`), and
`git diff --check` is clean. The geometry, drift and default-runtime test counts
from the previous checkpoint are not counted as fresh runs here. No production
GPU collider guard was removed, and no mixed joint/contact, performance or
whole-workspace certification is implied.

The replay also exposed a separate precision limitation: the CPU oracle rejects
some rounded GPU Gram matrices as indefinite, while rebuilding the physical Gram
in f64 from the sampled geometry yields a valid solve. This does not establish a
general PSD/rank/scale correction; that broader response-assembly gate stays open.

## P4 halt-safe contact publication prerequisite

Runtime bridge inspection found a publication hazard in the test-wired contact
route: contact response retires its scratch outputs after a sticky fault or
break-stop, but an unconditional copy can still replace accepted generalized
rates with those cleared outputs. A separate retained publication pass now gates
normal-force and corrected-rate copies on the shared device status.

- `contact_publication_gpu.rs` and `contact_publication.wgsl` provide
  `ResidentContactPublication` with prepared buffer-prefix bindings. All nonzero
  statuses suppress writes; the pass does not clear status or alter unbound tails.
  Storage usage, capacity, prefix alignment/length and writable aliases are
  validated before preparation. Encoding uses retained pipeline/bind groups and
  performs no host status polling.
- The existing loaded-trajectory fixtures use this pass for both publication
  points and bind Featherstone to the same status as geometry/contact processing.
  Per-substep queue submissions remain; this does not add public runtime contacts.
- Publication is not frame rollback: an error after an earlier accepted pass still
  requires restoring the frame checkpoint. Restitution, sleep/wake, reactions,
  material/topology mutation, compensation across frame uploads and mixed
  joint/contact solving remain separate bridge work. The production collider
  rejection remains intact.

Validation on the recorded RTX 4080 environment:

```sh
NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c make test-primitives-contact-publication-gpu
NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c make test-primitives-contact-response-gpu
NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c nixVulkan make test \
  APP_TARGET='-p molla-solvers --features gpu --lib contact_response_gpu::tests::contact_ -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1'
NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c make check-all
```

- Publication lane: **2 GPU tests pass**. Coverage includes all 32 individual
  status bits, combined faults, repeated break-stop, explicit reset, 257/129-word
  multi-workgroup prefixes, bit-preserving copies, untouched destination/status
  tails, invalid indices and preparation validation.
- Response lane: **8 GPU tests pass** with guarded publication/shared status.
  Holding, slide, reversal and all four breakaway resolutions retain the preceding
  checkpoint's measured errors and unchanged acceptance bounds. The lane completed
  in 420.34 seconds; this is not a production performance measurement.
- Follow-up: **2 GPU tests pass**, one extending the already-run fault test and
  one new predictor/redrift test (**11 unique GPU tests** across this checkpoint).
  Real response faults and break-stop retire scratch without replacing predicted
  rates. Four halted ping-pong steps preserve body poses/velocities, generalized
  coordinates/rates and both compensation buffers byte-for-byte; clearing status
  resumes integration. The follow-up was run after adding these assertions, not
  counted as part of the earlier eight-test invocation.
- Final `make check-all` and `git diff --check` pass. No whole-workspace test or
  production-contact acceptance is claimed. Logs: `publication-gpu.log`,
  `publication-response.log`, `publication-halt.log`, `publication-build.log`,
  `publication-check.log` under `benchmarks/primitives/contact-gpu-2026-09-28/`.

## P4 public GPU contact-runtime bridge

`RigidWorld::from_scene_gpu` now owns the retained bounds -> LBVH refit -> narrow
phase -> normal forces -> Featherstone predictor -> coupled contact response ->
status-guarded rate publication -> redrift route. This supersedes the historical
blanket collider rejection above, not the remaining P4/P5/P6 acceptance gates.

Implementation:

- `rigid_contacts_gpu.rs` prepares contact kernels and per-state publication groups,
  maintains a separate external-wrench buffer, and snapshots normal rows, tangent
  impulses, island mappings and disk regimes without substep host readback.
  Frame-boundary decoding publishes `ContactForce` samples through the existing
  solver/readout API and stable runtime collider/body handles.
- `GpuContactCapacity` configures pair and per-island tangent slots through
  `RigidWorld::from_scene_gpu_with_contact_capacity`. The default constructor uses
  64 pairs and 64 tangent contacts per island. Overflow remains a sticky device
  fault and rolls the frame back. Frame readback capacity grows for larger substep
  counts and is reused when counts shrink.
- Model-stamp changes rebuild geometry, material and collision-permission bindings.
  Coordinate/FK-position residues survive unchanged frame-boundary high-state
  uploads. Coordinate/pose edits reset them; device checkpoints restore them after
  an unsuccessful frame while retaining the compiled contact pipeline. External
  force/velocity changes alone do not discard coordinate residues.
- The runtime rejects host contact-filter callbacks rather than ignoring them.
  Authored scene collision permissions remain device-consumed. Contact scenes with
  distance/cone/scalar constraint impulses, joint breaking,
  sleeping/automatic settling or nonzero restitution still return explicit errors.
  Reaction capture is supported by the subsequent checkpoint below.
  Existing body damping, unsupported shape, control and actuator limitations remain.
- Runtime diagnostics include contact readback bytes. The existing bind-group field
  explicitly counts Featherstone/distance/reaction groups, not total contact
  resources; no complete allocation/performance certification is asserted.

The first live-runtime fixture failed with EPA fault 8 on shallow sphere-box
contacts (`runtime-contact-first.log`). It was not replaced by a plane fixture.
The resident narrow phase now uses analytic sphere-box closest features, including
interior, edge and corner cases, reversed endpoints and compensated relative
translations. General convex GJK/EPA is unchanged and can still fault. All 14
resident narrow-phase tests pass, including the new analytic regression at three
scales and large offsets with penetrations carried only in translation low bits
(`runtime-contact-narrow.log`).

The initial four public-runtime tests passed (`runtime-contact-analytic.log`).
The extended final checks also pass:

- **30 unique GPU tests pass:** 14 resident narrow-phase, 6 public contact-runtime
